 "body": "### Motivation\n- Resolve review 5267341343 without broadening the comparator scope: the QPBT closure must not contain a module-qualified private `ldSpaceSplit`, and split `--write` generation must honor optional or temporarily absent header/footer parts.\n- Preserve the four registered headline statements, their raw prescribed-answer Pauli effects, and the original LDT comparator fixture.\n\n### Description\n- Make the formalization-only `MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldSpaceSplit` equivalence public without changing its body or any public theorem signature, then regenerate the 31-file QPBT tree from freshly built target-module metadata. The generated mirror now carries the public kernel name; the known compiler-generated private completeness auxiliary remains a pending comparator diagnostic.\n- Make split assembly omit `null` or configured-but-missing header/footer files while retaining the generated split-module imports. Checked `--update` still refuses a configured missing part, and the existing path and header validation remains unchanged.\n- Add split-specific regressions for unconfigured parts, a missing configured header, and a missing configured footer.\n- Refresh once onto published main `f976bec2c15013b03840f6b34b743d36a67a1d5a`; preserve the LDT fixture byte-for-byte at SHA-256 `cbe5642bb88db75f86bd79936896e684aa407a02108d8259ead71a0738783e73`.\n\n### Testing\n- `lake env lean MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameMeasurements.lean`\n- `lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.LowDegreeGameTheorems MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.Soundness MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.QubitForm MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.Completeness` (9,285 jobs)\n- `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_assemble_challenge scripts.tests.test_comparator_challenge_config scripts.tests.test_comparator_challenge_drift scripts.tests.test_completion_gate` (97 tests)\n- Both `ldt` and `qpbt` drift checks passed; QPBT remains 31 files and only its `LowDegreeGameMeasurements` mirror changed.\n- A disposable manifest-pinned challenge project built `Challenge` successfully (8,686 jobs). Exactly the four challenge-root theorem stubs contain `sorry`; child modules and the edited library file contain none.\n- Normal commit hooks passed 867 tests with 9 expected skips and all statement-integrity, proof-debt, conclusion-shaped-hypothesis, unfaithful-marker, and explicit-axiom audits.\n\nPending verification: official all-four comparator equality, including the known generated completeness auxiliary; real landrun with nanoda; final-head local CI and independent review; and a verified merged-main library pin. This PR does not claim comparator acceptance.\n\n---\nAddresses #662\n",

 "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: qpbt-headline-raw-pauli-effects-20260921 -->\n### Motivation\n\nThe independent scout `scout-123-20260921-01` audited main commit\n`05df4b74fea7d291050909102c737e6b03d85ba6` and reported a headline statement\ndiscrepancy. The paper compares the direct Pauli-question effects, while the\nLean distances use complete measurements obtained by sending malformed answers\nto outcome zero. Rejection by the game does not make those effects zero.\n\nSource: `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex`,\n`thm:pauli` and `cor:pauli-binary`, lines 1426-1487; proof in\n`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1876`.\nRelevant Lean definitions are in `Test/SoundnessDefs.lean`, `Test/QubitForm.lean`,\nand `Test/PauliBasisTest.lean` (`pauliAnswerOrZero`).\n\n### Work\n\nValidate the discrepancy against the source and the existing proof API.\nIf confirmed, prove the rejected-answer mass bound and the transfer from the\ncompleted family to the direct effects for both players, including outcome zero.\nExpose the source-faithful conclusions in both headline theorems and absorb\nuniversal constants into the existing existential robustness parameters.\nPreserve useful completed-family lemmas as internal results where needed.\n\nAn explicit proved identification with the paper's answer parsing is also\nacceptable if it actually establishes the source conclusion. A documentation\nchange alone, an extra public hypothesis, or a weakened conclusion does not\ndischarge this issue. Record the precise mathematical comparison in the gap\nregister, update blueprint claims and direct consumers, and finish with a\nstatement-integrity audit. No new proof holes, axioms, or bypasses.\n\n### Acceptance\n\n- Both headline statements compare the paper's operator families.\n- All required transfer estimates are proved from the original hypotheses.\n- The axiom audit remains exactly the standard Lean axioms.\n- Focused checks, complete CI, and a fresh independent review pass.\n- Comparator regeneration is coordinated after the repaired public statements\n  stabilize; PRs #663 and #660 are owned separately and must not be edited here.\n\nThe scout also reports stale README, theorem-index, and blueprint claims.\nThose reviewer-document synchronization findings remain part of artifact\ncompletion and must be checked against this mathematical repair.",

 "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: qpbt-completion-register-blueprint-20260921 -->\n### Motivation\n\nThe completion gate proposed in PR #647 at\n`1e88ff948511d117d162d5a074cf14ade72078db` was run against published main\n`d7a38d929a901fd9651ab4f4d9c0c7a20162bae0` on 2026-09-21. C1 passed and C2\nfound the four headline audit commands. Two other findings require a focused\nmathematical documentation pass:\n\n- C3: `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt-gap-register.md` has no `Terminal status` column.\n- C4: 11 of 528 linked blueprint nodes have neither a formalization mark nor\n  a justified exemption. The exemption table is absent.\n\nThese are findings of the candidate gate, not a completion certificate.\nPreserve the semantics and adoption conditions of the completion protocol;\ndo not alter the gate to hide an unmet requirement.\n\n### Work\n\nRead each paper-gap note, its cited source, the corresponding blueprint\nstatement and the current Lean declarations. For each register row determine\nwhether it is `no-difference`, an adopted `corrected` statement satisfying\ncorrectness, sufficiency, minimality and Lean convergence, or still genuinely\nopen. Add the terminal-status field only with evidence for each classification.\nAn open obligation cannot be made terminal by renaming it or merely documenting\nthat it is unproved. Reconcile omitted notes and stale source/proof status\nclaims while preserving their history and useful mathematical content.\n\nAudit these unmarked linked nodes:\n\n- `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex`: `def:canonical-complement`,\n  `lem:canonical-complement`, `def:generalized-pauli`,\n  `lem:pauli-observable-expansion`.\n- `ch12_qpbt_games.tex`: `def:cl-func`, `def:cl-dist`,\n  `def:typed-cl-functions`, `def:typed-cl-distributions`.\n- `ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`: `lem:qld-xz-lines`, `def:combine-map`,\n  `lem:qld-4-13`.\n\nAdd a formalization mark only where the source/blueprint and Lean match.\nOtherwise provide the precise, defensible exemption allowed by the protocol,\nwith its mathematical scope and source-gap reference. A source theorem with a\nmissing load-bearing proof is not exempt merely to obtain a green gate.\nIdentify and separate any necessary mathematical construction instead of\ninventing proof evidence or enlarging the public theorem's assumptions.\n\n### Ownership and acceptance\n\nCoordinate with #665, which owns the raw Pauli-effect headline repair and its\nnecessary gap/blueprint updates. Issue #666 owns final README, theorem-index\nand general status prose; PR #650 owns the deviations page. Do not duplicate\nthose writers or modify the parked infrastructure work.\n\nThe final register and blueprint findings must be resolved on mathematical\nevidence, not only string checks. Run the gate, blueprint rendering and the\nblueprint axiom audit, followed by CI and fresh independent review. If a genuine\nobligation remains, report its exact source and Lean target and keep completion\nopen. The source corrections adopted in PRs #633/#634 do not authorize new\nweakenings elsewhere.",

 "body": "### Motivation\n- Fix the discrepancy tracked by #665: `thm:pauli` and `cor:pauli-binary` compare the raw prescribed-answer effects, while the previous Lean headline used a completed family that folded malformed answers into outcome zero.\n\n### Description\n- Add raw Pauli operator distances and prove completed-to-raw transfer estimates for Alice and Bob from fixed-edge rejection bounds and the transported-state estimate.\n- Absorb the additional linear and squared errors into the existential `deltaQld` prefactor, preserving the printed error form and full nonnegative error domain.\n- Update the qubit and nonvacuity consumers, blueprint proof account, theorem index, and paper-gap register.\n- Regenerate the QPBT comparator fixture. The first normal update failed with `stale context tables for challenge qpbt \u2014 unmatched extras keys: []; unmatched module_preludes scopes: ['MIPStarRE/Quantum/Measurement.lean:52', 'MIPStarRE/Quantum/Measurement.lean:96']`; the two stale QPBT-only preludes were removed because the raw headline closure no longer contains either completed postprocessing declaration. No target count or assembler logic changed.\n- Align the handwritten two-target QPBT challenge footer with the public raw-distance theorem; no completed-distance declarations or extra targets are added.\n\n### Statement integrity audit\n- Paper assumptions: admissible `(q,m,d)`, nonnegative `\u03b5`, and strategy value at least `1 - \u03b5`.\n- Lean assumptions: the same, with the existing fixed finite-field model as a faithful representation boundary.\n- Paper conclusion: local isometries and an auxiliary unit state satisfying the state estimate and both players' raw Pauli-effect estimates over `u \u2208 F_q^M`.\n- Lean conclusion: the same raw `.effect (.pauliOutcome u)` estimates for Alice and Bob with the same `deltaQld` form; no extra premise and no weakened conclusion.\n- Verdict: source-faithful. Only the existential universal prefactor is enlarged to absorb the transfer loss.\n\n### Testing\n- `lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.QubitForm MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.NonVacuity`\n- `lake env lean MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/RawOperatorTransfer.lean`\n- Direct `#print axioms` checks for the raw transfer, both headline theorems, and the honest-strategy consumer: only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.\n- `leanblueprint web`\n- `python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root . --challenge qpbt --update`\n- `python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root . --challenge qpbt`\n- `python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root . --challenge ldt`\n- `lake env lean /tmp/ChallengeQPBT-issue665.lean` after copying the regenerated expected challenge outside the worktree; it type-checks with only the two intentional challenge `sorry` warnings.\n- `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_comparator_challenge_drift`\n- Normal pre-commit and checked pre-push hooks.\n\n---\nCloses #665\n",

 "body": "### Motivation\n- Refresh the reviewer-facing deviations snapshot after PR #668 proved the completed-to-raw Pauli-effect transfer identified in review 5262974908.\n- Keep issue #637's documentation aligned with the current source without claiming completion of the wider artifact.\n\n### Description\n- Cover all 21 current QPBT paper-gap notes, including `qpbt_raw-pauli-effects.tex`, and explain both the former completed-family mismatch and the proved transfer to the raw prescribed-answer effects required by `thm:pauli` and `cor:pauli-binary`.\n- Update the source snapshot, counts, Lean locators, links, headline theorem description, and remaining source-route obligations. The page distinguishes faithful boundary hypotheses, unasserted printed claims, corrected statements, and statement-preserving alternative proofs or representations.\n- Retain the existing `texra-blueprint.toml` repository URL retarget. The PR diff remains limited to `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` and `texra-blueprint.toml`.\n\n### Testing\n- `texra-blueprint --root . paper-gaps check` (passes; reports existing advisory verdict-marker warnings)\n- Focused row/note/register bijection and Markdown link/anchor checks: 21 rows, 21 notes, 19 register rows, and 42 valid local links\n- Focused comparator/count checks: 8 printed-claim hits, 3 prose proof-debt regex hits, 16 `sorryAx` mentions, and 672/680 Lean file counts\n- Focused raw-effect, headline declaration, and paper-source locator checks\n- TOML parse and repository URL assertions\n- `git diff --check`\n- `lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.NonVacuity MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.QubitForm` to refresh the worktree's pre-PR-#668 compiled dependencies after the checked push detected stale `.olean` files\n- `lake env lean` on the five Lean files changed upstream since this PR's prior public head: `NonVacuity.lean`, `QubitForm.lean`, `Soundness.lean`, `Soundness/RawOperatorTransfer.lean`, and `SoundnessDefs.lean`\n- No full `lake build` or blueprint build was run because this PR itself changes no Lean source or blueprint chapter/declaration links.\n\n---\nAddresses #637\n",

     2

     4	Pauli basis test** of *MIP\* = RE* ([arXiv:2001.04383](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.04383)),
     5	together with the classical **low individual degree test** it is built on
     6	(*Quantum soundness of the classical low individual degree test*,
     7	[arXiv:2009.12982](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.12982)). The source sections are
     8	mirrored in-repo under `references/`; the Pauli basis test is developed in

    10

    19	## What is formalized
    20	
    21	The Pauli basis test is a two-player nonlocal game whose soundness is one of the
    22	rigidity ingredients of *MIP\* = RE*. The headline results:
    23	
    24	| Result | Lean declaration | File |
    25	|---|---|---|
    26	| Soundness of the Pauli basis test (blueprint `thm:pauli`) | `pauli_soundness` | `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness.lean:52` |

    31	`pauli_soundness` states: there are constants `a ≥ 1` and `0 < b < 1` such that
    32	for every admissible parameter tuple `P` and every `ε ≥ 0`, every strategy for

    34	auxiliary state under which the strategy's state is within
    35	`deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q` of the ideal state, and both players' operator
    36	families are within the same bound of the ideal Pauli observables. The error
    37	scale carries the admissible sizes as explicit arguments —
    38	`deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ)`, `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/SoundnessDefs.lean:35` —

    41	`q^(-b)` and `2^(-b·m·d)` terms express. As in the source, the constants are
    42	existentially quantified and no regime in which `deltaQld < 1` is exhibited;
    43	see [`docs/DEVIATIONS.md`](docs/DEVIATIONS.md).

    73	  thousands of lines.

    75	  `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` and on nothing else. There is no
    76	  dedicated Pauli-test axiom-audit module yet — the existing
    77	  [`MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean`](MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean)
    78	  covers the classical low-degree track only — so the check is made by asking
    79	  Lean directly; the command is under "Build and check" below. Repository-wide,
    80	  the pre-push gate (`.githooks/pre-push`) runs
    81	  [`scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py`](scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py)
    82	  `--ci`, which runs `#print axioms` on every blueprint declaration marked
    83	  `\leanok` and fails if any of them depends on `sorryAx`.
    84	- **Statement corrections are documented, not hidden.** Where the source
    85	  paper's printed statement is wrong, or where its printed proof does not
    86	  establish the printed claim, the deviation is recorded rather than papered
    87	  over. There are 20 Pauli-test gap notes (45 notes in total; the directory
    88	  also holds `command.tex`, `template.tex`, `policy.tex` and
    89	  `proof-gap-protocol.tex`, which are not notes) under
    90	  `docs/paper-gaps/`, summarized in the register linked below. Two printed
    91	  claims that are not established are carried as `Prop`-valued definitions
    92	  which state the source sentence without asserting it, so the printed form
    93	  stays visible and stays unproved.
    94	- **Independent checking.** There is no comparator challenge for
    95	  `pauli_soundness` yet. What can be re-checked outside this repository today
    96	  is the classical low individual degree test underneath: the statement
    97	  `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` has a challenge repository at
    98	  [LionSR/LDT-comparator](https://github.com/LionSR/LDT-comparator), which
    99	  re-declares the statement against Mathlib alone and runs the Lean comparator
   100	  against this library; the setup is described in
   101	  [`docs/comparator.md`](docs/comparator.md), and the template it is assembled
   102	  from lives under `scripts/comparator/`. The analogous challenge for the
   103	  Pauli statement has not been built: `Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator` is so far a
   104	  placeholder holding only a licence and a toolchain pin.

   106	## Build and check
   107	
   108	Install [elan](https://github.com/leanprover/elan); it reads `lean-toolchain`
   109	and fetches Lean `v4.32.0` automatically. From the repository root:
   110	
   111	```bash
   112	lake exe cache get              # fetch the pinned Mathlib build cache (required)
   113	lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT       # build the Pauli basis test development
   114	lake build MIPStarRE            # build everything (QPBT, LDT, Quantum)
   115	```
   116	
   117	To reproduce the axiom claim, ask Lean for the axiom closure of a headline
   118	declaration:
   119	
   120	```bash
   121	lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.Soundness
   122	printf 'import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.Soundness\n#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness\n' > AxiomCheck.lean
   123	lake env lean AxiomCheck.lean
   124	```
   125	
   126	`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` are the only axioms that should
   127	appear; in particular `sorryAx` must not. The same recipe applies to the other
   128	three headline declarations, with their own modules imported.
   129	
   130	To type-check a single file, which is the fastest iteration loop:
   131	
   132	```bash
   133	lake env lean MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness.lean
   134	```

    26	
    27	**Lean declaration** — fully qualified name, with the file and line it is
    28	declared at in this commit. Permalink base:
    29	
    30	```
    31	https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/blob/838c51b78f30b2dc8b0d9c696ce6f4970731f733/<file>#L<line>
    32	```
    33	
    34	**Paper** — file and line range under `references/qpbt-paper/`, given as the
    35	enclosing LaTeX environment, together with the source's own theorem/lemma label
    36	when it has one. Chapter files are abbreviated:
    37	
    38	| short | file under `references/qpbt-paper/` |
    39	|---|---|
    40	| `04` | `04_preliminaries.tex` |
    41	| `06` | `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex` |
    42	| `08` | `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex` |
    43	| `14` | `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex` |
    44	
    45	A dash means the source states the content as unlabelled prose with no
    46	environment to cite; the blueprint node then carries the reference.
    47	
    48	**Blueprint** — the node label and its location under `blueprint/src/chapter/`,
    49	given as the line that carries the node's `\label{…}`. Chapter files are
    50	abbreviated `ch11`–`ch16` after their `blueprint/src/chapter/chNN_qpbt_*.tex`
    51	file names. The pairing is not guessed: it is the node's own `\lean{…}` tag.
    52	`stmt`/`proof` record whether that node carries a statement-level and a
    53	proof-level `\leanok`.
    54	
    55	**Ax** — the axioms the declaration depends on, from `#print axioms`:
    56	
    57	- **S** = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, the three standard Lean
    58	  axioms. No `sorryAx`, and no project axiom: the Lean tree declares none.
    59	- **P** = `[propext]` only.
    60	
    61	Section 8 gives the raw probe output and the command that regenerates it.
    62	
    63	**Differs?** — whether the Lean statement departs from the printed one:
    64	
    65	- **no** — the Lean statement is the printed statement.
    66	- **correction: `note`** — a documented statement correction; `note` is a file
    67	  under [`docs/paper-gaps/`](paper-gaps/), and the row is also a row of
    68	  [`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt-gap-register.md`](paper-gaps/qpbt-gap-register.md).
    69	- **hypothesis: …** — the Lean statement adds the named hypothesis.
    70	- **support** — a formalization-support declaration with no separate statement
    71	  in the paper: an intermediate step, an obstruction, or a bridge between two

  1703		&V_\alice \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\alice^\dagger \\
  1704	  =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1705	  &\hspace{24em}\tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1706		 =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1707		 =& \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''}\;,
  1708	\end{align*}
  1709	where in the third line we used the (anti-)commutation relation
  1710	\[
  1711		\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \;.
  1712	\]
  1713	An entirely analogous calculation shows that $V_\bob \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\bob^\dagger = \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\bob ''}$.
  1714	
  1715	Next, from the self-consistency property of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ specified in \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1716	\[
  1717		\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right)^\dagger \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1718	\]
  1719	which, since $\tilde{W}^j$ is Hermitian, is equivalent to
  1720	\begin{equation}
  1721	\label{eq:qld-unitary-1}
  1722	\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;.
  1723	\end{equation}
  1724	Let $\ket{\vartheta} = V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}$, and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$ define the operator
  1725	\begin{align*}
  1726		H_W &= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \otimes \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1727			&= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} \\
  1728			&= \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \otimes \tau^W(s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits}
  1729	\end{align*}
  1730	where in the second line we used that for all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$, $\tau^W(\tilde{u}) = \bigotimes_{i = 1}^\nqubits \tau^W(\tilde{u}_i)$ with $\tau^W(\tilde{u}_i)$ being the generalized Pauli $W$ observable acting on the $i$-th qudit. In the third line, we used the fact that for every fixed $j$, we have $\E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) = \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \otimes \tau^W(s)$. \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-1} is then equivalent to 
  1731	\[
  1732		\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;,
  1733	\]
  1734	for $W \in \{X,Z\}$. 
  1735	
  1736	Observe that
  1737	\begin{align*}
  1738		\E_{s,s'} \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') &= \E_{s,s'} \sum_{a,b \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(as')} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes (-1)^{\tr(bs')} \ketbra{b+s}{b} \\
  1739		&= \E_{s} \sum_{a\in \F_q} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes \ketbra{a+s}{a} \\
  1740		&= \proj{\EPR_q}
  1741	\end{align*}
  1742	where to go from the first to the second line we used \Cref{lem:cancellation}. This implies that $H_X H_Z = \Big ( \E_{s,s' \in \F_q} \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} = \ketbra{\EPR_q}{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1743	By the triangle inequality, we have
  1744	\[
  1745		\left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\| \leq \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_X \ket{\vartheta} \right\| + \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|\;.
  1746	\]
  1747	Note that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1748	\[
  1749		\left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_W \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2 = 1 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} \leq 2 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1750	\]
  1751	where in the inequality we used that $H_W \leq \Id$. Furthermore,
  1752	\begin{align*}
  1753		\bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} &=\| H_W \ket{\vartheta} \|^2\\
  1754		 &= \| \ket{\vartheta} + (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \\
  1755		 &\geq (\|\ket{\vartheta}\| - \| (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|)^2 \\
  1756		 &\geq (1 - \delta_S)^2 \\
  1757		 &\geq 1 - 2\delta_S\;. 
  1758	\end{align*}
  1759	Therefore 
  1760	\begin{align*}
  1761	2\sqrt{\delta_S} &\geq \left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2  \\
  1762	&= \bra{\vartheta} H_X^2 \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_Z^2 \ket{\vartheta} - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1763	&\geq 2 - 4\delta_S - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \;,
  1764	\end{align*}
  1765	which implies that 
  1766	\[
  1767		\bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S} \;.
  1768	\]
  1769	Define the unnormalized state $\ket{\aux_0}$ on the registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ as
  1770	\[
  1771		\ket{\aux_0}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} = (\bra{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''} \cdot \ket{\vartheta}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''}
  1772	\]
  1773	and define the normalized state $\ket{\aux} = \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \ket{\aux_0}$. 
  1774	The inner product between $\ket{\vartheta}$ and $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$ can thus be evaluated as
  1775	\begin{align*}
  1776		\bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) &= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux_0} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) \\
  1777		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1778		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|^2 \\
  1779		&= \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \| \\
  1780		&\geq \sqrt{1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S}} \\
  1781		&\geq 1 - O(\sqrt{\delta_S})\;.
  1782	\end{align*}
  1783	This implies $\| \ket{\vartheta} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, which establishes the first item of the lemma.
  1784	
  1785	We now establish the second item of the lemma. In what follows, all $\simeq$ and $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$. From \Cref{lem:qld-win-implications} we have the following implications: for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1786		\begin{align}
  1787		\label{eq:qld-unitary-2}
  1788		M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} &\simeq_\eps \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a\;, \\
  1789		\label{eq:qld-unitary-3}
  1790		\Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a &\simeq_\eps  M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''}\;,
  1791		\end{align}
  1792		where $M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h$. 
  1793	From \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that
  1794		\begin{equation}
  1795		\label{eq:qld-unitary-4}
  1796			M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;.
  1797		\end{equation}
  1798	Using \Cref{fact:triangle-for-simeq} with Equations \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-2}, \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-3}, and \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-4}, we get 
  1799		\begin{equation}
  1800			\label{eq:qld-unitary-5}
  1801			M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_S}} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;,
  1802		\end{equation}
  1803		where we used that $\delta_S \geq \eps$. 
  1804		
  1805		Next, we have for all $u \in \F_q^m$ 
  1806		\begin{align}
  1807			&V_\bob \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \notag \\
  1808			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))    \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1809			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_h   \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1810			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1811		= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1812	= &\Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''}\;,		\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}
  1813		\end{align}
  1814		where in the second line we expanded out the definitions of $V_\bob$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ (defined in \cref{eq:tilde_M}); in the third line we expanded out the definition of $\tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))$ (defined in \cref{eq:def-tauwu}) and used the fact that for all $h \in \F_q^M$, the inner product $h \cdot \ind_m(u)$ is equal to $g_h(u)$; in the fourth line we used the identities
  1815		\[
  1816			\tau^X(s) \tau^Z_h \tau^X(s)^\dagger = \tau^Z_{h + s} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \tau^Z(s) \tau^X_h \tau^Z(s)^\dagger = \tau^X_{h + s}~;
  1817		\]
  1818		and in the fifth line is due to the following short calculation: for all fixed $g_W$ we have
  1819		\begin{align*}
  1820			\sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a}  \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) - g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) + g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h': g_{h'}(u) = a} \tau^W_{h'}~.
  1821		\end{align*}
  1822		The second equality from the fact that $\F_q$ is a field of characteristic $2$ (so subtraction is the same as addition), and the third equality follows from the fact that letting $h' = h + \coded(g_W)$, we have $g_{h'} = g_h + g_W$ (in other words, the low-degree encoding $h \mapsto g_h$ is linear in $h$). 
  1823		
  1824		
  1825	
  1826	
  1827	Let $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. We show that $V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}$ (the argument for the operators acting on registers $\bob \bob' \bob''$ proceeds identically). 
  1828		\begin{align}
  1829			&\sum_h \bra{\Delta} \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}  \right)^\dagger \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \right) \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1830			&= 2 - 2 \Re \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice\, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1831			&= 2 - 2 \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-7}
  1832	\end{align}
  1833		where in the last line we used that $(\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} = (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1834		We now claim that
  1835		\begin{align}
  1836		&  \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \notag \\
  1837		&\approx_{md/q}  \E_u \sum_{\substack{h, h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-8} \\
  1838		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1839		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes V_\bob  \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-9}
  1840		\end{align}
  1841		where the equality in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9} follows from the identity in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-6}, and the approximation in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-8} follows from the following calculation:
  1842		\begin{align*}
  1843			& \E_u \sum_{\substack{h \neq h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \\
  1844			&= \sum_{h \neq h'} \left( \E_u \mathbf{1}[g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)] \right) \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \\
  1845			&\leq \frac{md}{q}\;.
  1846		\end{align*}
  1847		In the last line we used that for for distinct $h \neq h'$, the polynomials $g_h \neq g_{h'}$ and thus by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma can only agree on at most $md/q$ fraction of points $u \in \F_q^m$. 
  1848		
  1849		Continuing from \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}, we use the first item of the Lemma which shows that $\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$ and equivalently $\| V_\alice^\dagger \otimes V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\hat{\psi}} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, so 
  1850		\begin{align*}
  1851			\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}} &\approx_{O(\delta_S^{1/4})} \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1852			&\geq 1 - O(\delta_S^{1/2})\;,
  1853		\end{align*}
  1854	        where the last line comes from \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-5}.
  1855		Together with \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}, 
  1856		\[
  1857		\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}} \leq O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)\;.	
  1858		\]
  1859		This concludes the proof of the second item of the lemma.
  1860	\end{proof}
  1861	
  1862	We now prove \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. 
  1863	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}]
  1864		Let $\strategy = (\psi,M)$ be a projective strategy for $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\alice \bob$. As mentioned at the beginning of \Cref{sec:commutation}, we assume that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is padded with sufficiently many ancilla $\ket{0}$ qubits. Let $\phi_\alice$ be the following isometry mapping the register $\alice$ to the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ where $\alice'$ and $\alice''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$:
  1865		\[
  1866			\phi_\alice: \ket{\theta}_\alice \mapsto V_\alice (\ket{\theta}_\alice \otimes (\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice' \alice''})
  1867		\]
  1868		where $V_\alice$ is the unitary acting on $\alice \alice' \alice''$ from \Cref{lem:qld-unitary}. Define the isometry $\phi_\bob$ analogously. \Cref{lem:qld-unitary} then implies that there exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1869		\[
  1870			\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld
  1871		\]
  1872		and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1873		\[
  1874			\phi_\alice \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\alice \, \phi_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \phi_\bob \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\bob \, \phi_\bob^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1875		\]
  1876		where the $\approx$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. This shows that $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ is a self-test for the strategy $\strategy^\pauli$ with robustness $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. We conclude the proof by making the identification of registers $\alice \alice'$ with $\alice'$ and $\bob \bob'$ with $\bob'$ to be consistent with the statement of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. We also note that, when unpacking the dependence on parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for some universal constants $a > 1, 0 < b < 1$, as desired.
  1877	\end{proof}

    14	/-!
    15	# Axiom audits for the quantum Pauli basis test
    16	
    17	Reviewer-facing, machine-checked evidence that the QPBT headline results rest on
    18	nothing beyond Lean's three standard axioms.  Before this module the claim was
    19	reproducible only by running a throwaway metaprogram outside the repository; a
    20	reader of the artifact could not re-derive it.
    21	
    22	Each audit below both **prints** the axiom set of a headline declaration and
    23	**fails elaboration** unless that set is exactly
    24	
    25	`{Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext}`.
    26	
    27	So the module is a compile-time regression test, not a report: if a `sorry`
    28	(`sorryAx`), a new `axiom` declaration, or any other unexpected dependency ever
    29	reaches one of these theorems, `lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.AxiomAudit`
    30	fails and CI goes red.  The printed lines remain in the build log as the
    31	positive record.
    32	
    33	This mirrors `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean`, which uses the same
    34	`Lean.collectAxioms` mechanism for the classical low-individual-degree track.
    35	Like that module, this one is built explicitly as a CI target rather than
    36	imported from the `MIPStarRE.QPBT` umbrella, so the audits stay out of normal
    37	downstream imports while still acting as regression tests.
    38	
    39	## What is audited
    40	
    41	The declarations are the QPBT headline results, in dependency order from the
    42	soundness statement down to the combining and extraction layers:

     5	/-!
     6	# Non-vacuity of the Pauli basis test soundness theorem
     7	
     8	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` is an implication: for every admissible
     9	parameter tuple `P`, every `ε ≥ 0` and every strategy `S` for
    10	`pauliBasisTest P` with `1 - ε ≤ S.value`, extraction data exist whose three
    11	error quantities are bounded by `deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q`.  A reader is
    12	entitled to ask two questions about such a statement, and this module answers
    13	both with citable declarations.  Nothing here changes or restates an existing
    14	definition or theorem; every result is a corollary of material already on the
    15	main development.
    16	
    17	## Q1 — are the hypotheses satisfiable?
    18	
    19	`AdmissibleParams` is inhabited (`nonVacuousParams`, and hence
    20	`nonempty_admissibleParams`), and for *every* admissible `P` the honest
    21	strategy of `lem:pauli-completeness` is a strategy for `pauliBasisTest P`
    22	itself with value exactly `1` (`exists_pauliBasisTest_strategy_value_one`);
    23	the symmetric presentation used by `exists_spcc_value_one` has
    24	`pauliBasisTest P` as its underlying game definitionally
    25	(`pauliBasisTestSymm_toGame`).  Consequently the hypothesis triple
    26	`0 ≤ ε`, `S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)`, `1 - ε ≤ S.value` is jointly
    27	satisfiable — with `ε = 0`, the strongest case
    28	(`pauli_soundness_hypotheses_satisfiable`) — and `pauli_soundness` applied to
    29	it yields an unconditional statement
    30	(`pauli_soundness_applies_to_honest_strategy`).
    31	
    32	## Q2 — is the conclusion non-trivial?
    33	
    34	The bound is `deltaQld a b ε m d q = a * (m*d)^a * (ε^b + q^(-b) + 2^(-b*m*d))`
    35	with `a, b` existentially quantified by the theorem, so no *single* numeric
    36	value can be extracted.  What can be shown, and is shown here, is that
    37	whatever the constants `a ≥ 1` and `0 < b < 1` produced by `pauli_soundness`
    38	are, the bound is not vacuously large: along the explicit admissible family
    39	`nonVacuousParams n` the error at `ε = 0` tends to `0`
    40	(`tendsto_deltaQld_nonVacuousParams`), so for every `η > 0` there are
    41	admissible parameters at which the soundness conclusion bounds all three
    42	distances by less than `η` (`exists_admissibleParams_deltaQld_lt` and the
    43	combined `pauli_soundness_nontrivial`).
    44	
    45	**What is *not* shown.** This is a statement about the `ε = 0` section of
    46	`deltaQld` for a *chosen* parameter family, not a uniform rate: it does not
    47	locate a threshold `ε₀ > 0` below which the bound is small for a *fixed*
    48	parameter tuple, and it does not compare `deltaQld` against the trivial bound
    49	on `rawPauliOperatorDistanceA`/`rawPauliOperatorDistanceB` at fixed
    50	parameters. It also does not assert anything about the numerical size of the
    51	constants `a` and `b`, which the source theorem leaves implicit
    52	(`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    53	Continuity of `deltaQld` in `ε` at `0` is recorded separately
    54	(`tendsto_deltaQld_eps_zero`) so that a reader can see that the `ε = 0`
    55	section is the limiting case of the `ε > 0` statement rather than a
    56	degenerate one.
    57

    60	Supports blueprint `thm:pauli` and `lem:pauli-completeness`; paper origin

    62	and `:1229-1421`.  This module is formalization-only bookkeeping: it states no
    63	new mathematics of the source and introduces no hypothesis.
    64	-/

    66	
    67	For Alice, rejection on the oriented Pauli-to-point edge bounds the state
    68	mass of $M_{\mathrm{malformed}}$ by

    70	the same bound for Bob.  If the transported strategy state is within

    55	\section{Key theorem forms}
    56	
    57	Three statements must be kept apart.  Throughout, $\game$ denotes a symmetric
    58	two-player one-round game and $\eps \ge 0$ a real parameter; the notation is
    59	introduced in the next section.
    60	
    61	\begin{enumerate}
    62	  \item \textbf{Source form (attainment form).}  If
    63	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and projective
    64	  strategy $\strategy$ with $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps$.
    65	  \item \textbf{Approximate form (what the source proof establishes).}  If
    66	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then for every $\eps' > \eps$ there exists a
    67	  symmetric and projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    68	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps'$.
    69	  \item \textbf{Given-strategy form (value-preserving symmetrization).}  If
    70	  $\strategy'$ is any strategy for $\game$ with
    71	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and
    72	  projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    73	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) = \val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$.
    74	\end{enumerate}
    75	
    76	The source proof consists exactly of a proof of the third form, applied to a
    77	strategy supplied by the definition of the supremum; this yields the second
    78	form.  The first form asserts strictly more than the second, and the passage
    79	from the second to the first is the gap discussed in this note.  Every use of
    80	the lemma, in the source and in this project, consumes only the second or the
    81	third form.
    82	
    83	\section{The source assertion}
    84	
    85	A two-player one-round game
    86	$\game = (\mathcal X, \mathcal A, \mu, D)$ in compact symmetric notation
    87	consists of a finite question alphabet $\mathcal X$, a finite answer alphabet
    88	$\mathcal A$, a symmetric question distribution $\mu$ on
    89	$\mathcal X \times \mathcal X$, and a decision predicate $D$ treating the two
    90	players symmetrically.  A tensor product strategy
    91	$\strategy = (\ket\psi, A, B)$ consists of a unit vector $\ket\psi$ in a
    92	tensor product $\mathcal H_A \ot \mathcal H_B$ of \emph{finite-dimensional}
    93	Hilbert spaces together with POVMs $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ for the two
    94	players; its value $\val^*(\game, \strategy)$ is the acceptance probability,
    95	and the value of the game is the supremum
    96	\begin{equation*}
    97	  \val^*(\game) = \sup_{\strategy} \val^*(\game, \strategy)
    98	\end{equation*}
    99	over all tensor product strategies.  A strategy is projective if all its
   100	measurements are projective, and symmetric if the state is
   101	permutation-invariant on $\mathcal H \ot \mathcal H$ and both players use the
   102	same measurements.
   103	
   104	The symmetrization lemma of \cite[Section~5]{Ji2020MIPStar} asserts:%
   105	\footnote{The statement is at
   106	\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~94--99,
   107	and its proof at lines~101--132.  The blueprint statement kept in this form
   108	is \path{lem:symmetric-strat} in
   109	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}.}
   110	if $\game$ is a symmetric game with $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some
   111	$\eps \ge 0$, then
   112	\begin{equation*}
   113	  \exists\, \strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M) \text{ symmetric and projective}
   114	  \quad\text{with}\quad
   115	  \val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps.
   116	  \tag{\path{lem:symmetric-strat}}
   117	\end{equation*}
   118	
   119	Its proof runs as follows.  For every $\eps' > \eps$ the definition of the
   120	supremum supplies a strategy $\strategy' = (\ket{\psi'}, A, B)$ with
   121	$\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps'$.  By Naimark dilation in the completed
   122	projective form of \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} one may take
   123	$\ket{\psi'} \in \C^d_{A'} \ot \C^d_{B'}$ for some integer $d$ with all
   124	measurements projective.  One then forms the permutation-invariant state
   125	\begin{equation*}
   126	  \ket{\psi} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}
   127	  \bigl( \ket{0}_A \ket{1}_B \ket{\psi'}_{A'B'}
   128	       + \ket{1}_A \ket{0}_B \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{A'B'} \bigr)
   129	\end{equation*}
   130	on $(\C^2 \ot \C^d) \ot (\C^2 \ot \C^d)$, where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ permutes
   131	the two players' registers, and the block-diagonal projective measurements
   132	$M^x_a = \ket{0}\!\bra{0} \ot A^x_a + \ket{1}\!\bra{1} \ot B^x_a$.  Symmetry
   133	of $D$ gives $\val^*(\game, (\ket\psi, M)) = \val^*(\game, \strategy')$.  The
   134	construction is therefore \emph{value-preserving}: applied to any strategy it
   135	produces a symmetric projective strategy of exactly the same value.  What the
   136	proof establishes is thus the given-strategy form, hence the approximate form;
   137	the printed conclusion is the attainment form.
   138	
   139	\section{Why attainment does not follow}
   140	
   141	The supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ ranges over strategies on
   142	finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces of unbounded dimension.  The strategies
   143	$\strategy'_{\eps'}$ produced for $\eps' \downarrow \eps$ may require
   144	dimensions $d(\eps')$ growing without bound, and there is no compactness
   145	across dimensions from which a limiting finite-dimensional strategy of value
   146	at least $1-\eps$ could be extracted.  A symmetric projective strategy of
   147	value at least $1-\eps = \val^*(\game)$ would attain the supremum, so the
   148	printed conclusion is equivalent, under its hypothesis, to the assertion that
   149	$\val^*(\game)$ is attained by some strategy.  No general principle supplies
   150	this: it is known, and recalled in the introduction of the source itself, that
   151	the set of finite-dimensional quantum correlations is not closed and differs
   152	from the set of infinite-dimensional spatial correlations, so limits of
   153	finite-dimensional strategies need not be realized by any finite-dimensional
   154	strategy.  Whether some symmetric game realizes the failure --- a game whose
   155	value is attained by no tensor product strategy, presented together with the
   156	exposing functional as a decision predicate --- is a separate question that
   157	this note does not need to settle.  The local verdict is about the proof: the
   158	cited argument proves the approximate form and does not prove the attainment
   159	form.
   160	
   161	\section{An additional obstruction in the formal domain}
   162	
   163	The current Lean structure for a symmetric game assumes finiteness of its
   164	answer alphabet but does not require that alphabet to be nonempty.  Consider
   165	the game with question alphabet $\mathcal X=\{*\}$, answer alphabet
   166	$\mathcal A=\varnothing$, the probability distribution concentrated on
   167	$(*,*)$, and the unique decision predicate on the empty answer domain.
   168	Both symmetry requirements hold.  There is no tensor product strategy for
   169	this game: a unit vector in $\mathcal H_A\ot\mathcal H_B$ forces both local
   170	spaces to be nonzero, whereas completeness of Alice's empty measurement
   171	would give
   172	\[
   173	  0=\sum_{a\in\varnothing} A^*_a=I_{\mathcal H_A},
   174	\]
   175	which is impossible on a nonzero space.
   176	
   177	Lean defines the game value using the conditional supremum operation on
   178	$\mathbb R$.  For the empty set this operation is assigned the value zero,
   179	as expressed by Mathlib's \leanid{Real.sSup\_empty}.  This is a convention
   180	outside the nonempty domain on which the usual least-upper-bound property
   181	holds; it is not an attainment principle.  Thus \leanid{Game.value} assigns
   182	the example the value $0=1-\eps$ with $\eps=1\geq0$, but it has no symmetric
   183	projective strategy, since it has no strategy at all.  Consequently the exact
   184	current Lean statement is false on its admitted domain, independently of the
   185	unbounded-dimension issue.  The complete verification and its axiom audit are
   186	recorded in \path{audits/2026-09-12_issue-524-symmetrization-obstruction.md}.%
   187	\footnote{The verification reuses the existing
   188	\leanid{nonempty\_of\_unit\_vector} and
   189	\leanid{measurement\_outcome\_nonempty} lemmas.  Its declarations depend only
   190	on \leanid{propext}, \leanid{Classical.choice}, and \leanid{Quot.sound},
   191	not on the unfinished symmetrization theorem.}
   192	
   193	This example concerns a boundary of the formal encoding.  Although the
   194	printed definition of a game lists finite alphabets without an explicit
   195	nonemptiness condition, it does not specify a real value for the supremum
   196	over an empty strategy class.  The example therefore does not establish
   197	nonattainment for the intended class of games with nonempty alphabets.
   198	Making that domain condition explicit would exclude this example but would
   199	leave the source proof's attainment step unproved.  The statement-integrity
   200	review requested here was carried out on 2026-09-19 and is the statement
   201	correction recorded below; the printed Lean statement and its proof-gap marker
   202	were replaced there by an unasserted Lean proposition and this refutation,
   203	proved as \leanid{not\_forall\_printedSymmetricProjectiveAttainmentClaim}.
   204	
   205	\section{Uses of the lemma}
   206	
   207	The source invokes the lemma twice.
   208	
   209	First, in the soundness proof for the oracularization transformation, the
   210	argument fixes a strategy $\strategy^{\mathrm{orac}}$ for the oracularized game
   211	``with value $1-\eps$'' and applies the lemma to assume without loss of
   212	generality that it is projective.%
   213	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/10_oracularization.tex},
   214	lines~317--321.}
   215	Here the input is a given strategy, not the value of the game; the
   216	given-strategy form applies verbatim and preserves the value exactly, so the
   217	use is justified by what the proof establishes.
   218	
   219	Second, in the soundness proof for answer reduction, the argument assumes the
   220	strict inequality $\val^*(\game) > 1-\eps$ and concludes that there is a
   221	symmetric projective strategy of value greater than $1-\eps$.%
   222	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/11_answer_reduction.tex},
   223	lines~2322--2332.}
   224	Writing $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps_0$ with $\eps_0 < \eps$ and applying the
   225	approximate form with $\eps' = (\eps+\eps_0)/2$ produces a symmetric
   226	projective strategy of value at least $1-\eps' > 1-\eps$.  A strict lower
   227	bound on the supremum thus passes through the approximate form; attainment is
   228	not used.
   229	
   230	In this project, the soundness statements of the Pauli basis test track
   231	quantify over strategies assumed to succeed with probability at least
   232	$1-\eps$, so any symmetrization step starts from a given strategy and consumes
   233	the given-strategy form.  The blueprint records both forms as part of the
   234	games vocabulary and has no downstream dependency on either; the two source
   235	uses above belong to transformations outside the scope of the present
   236	development.
   237	Consequently, no consumer of the lemma --- in the source or here --- requires
   238	the attainment form.

    68	\section{Key theorem forms}
    69	
    70	Throughout, $(q,m,d)$ is an admissible parameter tuple of the Pauli basis
    71	test, $\ket{\hat\psi}$ is the expanded state of the projective strategy
    72	under analysis, succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, and all
    73	approximations are with respect to $\ket{\hat\psi}$.  For lines
    74	$\ell_X, \ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$, the POVM $\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$,
    75	with outcomes pairs of polynomials of degree at most $md$ on the two
    76	lines, is the two-basis combined line measurement, and
    77	$\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ is the combined point measurement; their
    78	consistency errors are $\delta_P = \poly(\eps, md/q)$ and
    79	$\delta_Q = \poly(\eps)$ respectively, and
    80	$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}} = \poly(\eps)$ is the line--point consistency
    81	error of the strategy.  The lemma under discussion asserts that a
    82	measurement $\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, built for each line $\ell$ in
    83	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, is $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$-consistent, on average over
    84	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$, with the combined point
    85	measurement on the extended coordinates, together with the
    86	register-swapped counterpart.%
    87	\footnote{In the mirror of the source consulted here,
    88	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}: the
    89	lemma statement, with the error form $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, is at
    90	lines~1020--1034 (label \path{lem:qld-4-13}); the central display with
    91	the first-route bound at lines~1134--1137
    92	(label \path{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}); the three claims at
    93	lines~1140--1239 (labels \path{claim:17-1}--\path{claim:17-3}); the
    94	second-route conclusion $O(m^2\delta_P)$ at lines~1241--1245, preceded by
    95	a duplicated sentence whose second copy carries a malformed reference;
    96	the product-distribution estimate invoked there at lines~1055--1061
    97	(label \path{eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted}); and the sub-line lemma at
    98	lines~1063--1116 (label \path{lem:qld-sublines}).}
    99	The comparison involves four forms of the error function
   100	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(\eps,m,d,q)$.
   101	\begin{enumerate}
   102	  \item \textbf{Source form.}
   103	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = \poly(m^2\eps,\, md/q)$.  This is the form
   104	  printed in the statement.  Neither printed derivation supports it.
   105	  \item \textbf{Established form (first route).}
   106	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}
   107	  = O\big(m\,(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4}
   108	  + \delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2})\big)$, a function of the form
   109	  $m \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)$.
   110	  \item \textbf{Second-route form (conditional).}
   111	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = O(m^2 \delta_P)
   112	  = m^2 \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)$, conditional on a joint-law
   113	  decomposition that the sub-line lemma, as stated, does not provide.
   114	  \item \textbf{Consumer requirement.}  The unique consumer, the
   115	  polynomial-pair lemma, feeds $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$ into an error
   116	  of the form
   117	  $a(md)^a(\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ imported
   118	  from \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}; any bound
   119	  $m^{O(1)} \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$ is absorbed by enlarging $a$ and
   120	  shrinking $b$, so forms~2 and~3 both suffice downstream.
   121	\end{enumerate}
   122	
   123	\section{The domain of the conditional Lean helper}
   124	
   125	The source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point measurement as an
   126	input.  It uses the family $\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ constructed by the preceding
   127	point lemma, whose error has the form $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.  Consequently,
   128	an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
   129	the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
   130	$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
   131	predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
   132	point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.
   133	
   134	Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
   135	\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
   136	order
   137	\[
   138	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   139	  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   140	  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
   141	  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   142	\]
   143	Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
   144	$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
   145	\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
   146	comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
   147	arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
   148	cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.
   149	
   150	There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
   151	$\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
   152	sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
   153	joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
   154	Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
   155	zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
   156	by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
   157	arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
   158	\path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at

# Comparator verification of the headline theorems

Two challenges are configured.  The LDT challenge targets
`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal`.  The QPBT challenge targets the four registered
QPBT results: `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one`,
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness`, and
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit`.  They share the generation tooling in
`scripts/comparator/`, the drift guard, and the trust model below; each lives in
its own challenge repository.

## The LDT challenge

The headline theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` (the corrected source
statement of `thm:main-formal` from the low individual degree test paper) is
independently verifiable with the official
[leanprover/comparator](https://github.com/leanprover/comparator), the
top level of the escalating checks in the Lean reference manual's
[Validating Proofs](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/ValidatingProofs/)
chapter.

Following community practice
([lamplighter-comparator](https://github.com/vidick/lamplighter-comparator),
[erdos-unit-distance-comparator](https://github.com/kim-em/erdos-unit-distance-comparator)),
the challenge lives in a separate repository —
**[LDT-comparator](https://github.com/LionSR/LDT-comparator)** —
which requires this library as a lake dependency pinned by commit:

- `Challenge.lean` there imports **only Mathlib** and re-declares, verbatim
  and in dependency order, every declaration in the comparator-relevant
  closure of the statement of `mainFormal` (111 declarations, ~1200 lines),
  then states the theorem with `sorry`.  It is the entire human audit
  surface.
- `Solution.lean` there imports this library, which proves the theorem under
  the same fully-qualified names; no bridging lemmas are needed.
- Its CI runs the comparator (real landrun sandbox, nanoda external kernel,
  `lean4checker` re-check) on every push and weekly.

## What this repository contributes

1. **Environment alignment.**  Comparator compares, constant by constant, the
   full kernel closure of the statement — types, definition bodies, and the
   proofs embedded in them — so `Challenge.lean` must elaborate to
   bit-identical terms.  Every module contributing a declaration to the
   closure therefore uses the full `import Mathlib` (directly or through
   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersBase.lean` /
   `MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`), so tactic elaboration sees
   the same environment as the Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`.  The four
   modules with direct Mathlib imports carry a comment saying not to narrow
   them.  (Measured impact: only 14 modules that did not already see full
   Mathlib through `Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean` gained it.)
2. **Regeneration tooling.**  `scripts/comparator/` holds the closure
   extractor (a Lean metaprogram mirroring comparator's `runForUsedConsts`)
   and the assembler that produce `Challenge.lean`.  After changing any
   definition in the closure: regenerate per `scripts/comparator/README.md`,
   copy the result into LDT-comparator, and bump its library pin.

## Checklist against the official *Validating Proofs* guide

| Level | Requirement | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | `#print axioms` shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` | `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean`; also enforced by comparator's `permitted_axioms` |
| 3 | `lean4checker --fresh` re-check | `lean4checker: true` in the comparator repo's lean-action step |
| 4 | Statement written in a trusted environment, separate from proof code | `Challenge.lean` imports only Mathlib (CI-enforced grep); separate repo, library pinned by commit |
| 4 | Sandboxed build + export + kernel replay | official comparator binary (pinned to the toolchain tag), real landrun in CI |
| 4 | External checker in addition to the Lean kernel | `enable_nanoda = true` (pinned nanoda tag); local macOS runs use `./verify.sh --fake-landrun` which disables it |
| 5 | No native evaluation (`Lean.trustCompiler`, `decide +native`) | excluded by `permitted_axioms` — comparator rejects any extra axiom |
| — | Statement review: custom notation and type classes must not obscure meaning | `Challenge.lean` uses no custom notation; review of it is the human step |

Deliberate deviations from the comparator README's adversarial setup, per its
own guidance for trusted trees: the `systemd-run` landrun-escape guard is
omitted and prebuilt `.lake` artifacts are reused, because both modules come
from a trusted checkout rather than an untrusted submitter.

Residual trust: Lean's logical soundness, comparator's own plumbing, sandbox
security, simultaneous bugs in all checkers, and human error in
`Challenge.lean` itself — keep that file short, notation-free, and reviewed.

## The QPBT challenge

The QPBT challenge is prepared for the separate repository
**[QPBT-comparator](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator)**.  Its current
configuration supplies these four theorem names to one comparator run:

- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one` (`lem:pauli-completeness`);
- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness` (`lem:ld-soundness`);
- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` (`thm:pauli`); and
- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` (`cor:pauli-binary`).

The checked-in generated tree is `scripts/comparator/expected/qpbt/`.  It has a
root `Challenge.lean` and thirty Mathlib-only mirror modules under `Challenge/`,
one for each contributing library module.  The root states all four targets
with `sorry`; the drift guard regenerates and byte-compares the complete tree
with `--challenge qpbt`.

### Current verification status

At library commit `a534c7f97ba34fd561ae03134f90b81ee4e395c1`, generation and
elaboration of this four-target tree passed, as did the canonical local CI
contexts.  Those checks establish that the generated challenge and library
compile.  They do **not** establish equality of every declaration in the union
of the four statement closures.  In particular, equality of the generated
private auxiliaries reached through the completeness target remains
unestablished.

The following checks are still pending for the four-target configuration:

- an official comparator run establishing all-four closure equality;
- equality of the private and compiler-generated completeness auxiliaries;
- real-landrun verification with nanoda enabled; and
- a challenge-repository pin to the verified commit after it reaches `main`.

There is a narrower historical result.  At commit
`4aec9ebedf6ca401e3f2d7b4bd90bd565d38f90d`, the split challenge configured
only `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` and
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit`.  On that exact two-target configuration,
`./verify.sh --fake-landrun` reported acceptance.  Fake landrun disables nanoda,
and that run did not include `exists_spcc_value_one` or `exists_ld_soundness`, so
it is not evidence for the current four-target challenge.

### Environment alignment for QPBT

Comparator compares the full kernel closure constant by constant, so each
Mathlib-only challenge module must elaborate to bit-identical terms.  The
library and generator use the following alignment measures:

1. **Full Mathlib imports.**  Four closure modules -
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Subspaces.lean`,
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Coefficients.lean`,
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/LowDegreeCode.lean`, and
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Lines.lean` - use the full `import Mathlib`, so tactic
   elaboration sees the same environment as the challenge modules.  Other
   closure modules receive Mathlib through existing shared imports.
2. **Public closure members.**  A `private` declaration's real name is qualified
   by its defining module (`_private.<module>.0.<name>`), so a challenge module
   cannot re-declare it under the library's name.  Closure members needed by the
   challenge were therefore made public without changing their statements,
   bodies, or proof scripts.
3. **Named local instances.**  The group and decidable-equality instances for
   the Galois group in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/FieldBasis.lean` have explicit
   names.  This avoids generated names that encode the defining module.
4. **Mirrored module partition.**  Lean caches nested proof and `match`
   auxiliaries per module, names them after the first declaration in that module
   that needs them, and limits instance synthesis to the module's imports.  The
   QPBT challenge therefore mirrors the source module partition and import
   graph.  This behavior is selected by `"split": true` in
   `scripts/comparator/challenges/qpbt.json`; `assemble_challenge.py --split-dir`
   writes the tree under `scripts/comparator/expected/qpbt/`.

The split layout also avoids adding QPBT-specific global instance wrappers to
`MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`.  The original LDT challenge bytes
are protected independently by the baseline regression described in
`scripts/comparator/README.md`.

No public statement of any of the four targets changed as part of this
comparator alignment.  Comparator equality remains pending as described above.

The "do not narrow this import" notes on the shared base modules
(`MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersBase.lean`,
`MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/Distribution.lean`,
`MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`) still name only `mainFormal`,
and deliberately so: those modules contribute to both closures, and adding a
line to a module docstring shifts every declaration below it, which would
rewrite the `-- source:` provenance comments of the checked-in LDT challenge.
They are covered by this section instead.

### Regenerating and auditing

Regeneration is the pipeline in `scripts/comparator/README.md` with
`--challenge qpbt`.  After an intentional change to any definition in the
closure: regenerate, copy the expected file into QPBT-comparator as
`Challenge.lean` and `Challenge/`, bump the `rev` pin in its `lakefile.toml`
and `lake-manifest.json` to the library commit they were generated from, and
run its `./verify.sh`.

What the human must audit, and what no tool can check: that the challenge
modules really state the intended theorems.  Concretely, that
the Pauli basis test it defines — `pauliQuestionDistribution`,
`pauliWinPredicate`, `pauliBasisTest` — is the test of the paper; that
`deltaQld` is the paper's error functional; that `PauliSoundnessWitness` and
`QubitSoundnessWitness` package isometries and an auxiliary state without
smuggling in a hypothesis; and that `Strategy.value` and the operator
distances mean what their names claim.  Agreement of the remaining declarations
is exactly what the pending four-target comparator run must establish.

## Benchmark use

The same statement is submission-ready for
[leanprover/lean-eval](https://github.com/leanprover/lean-eval) (the official
comparator-based benchmark behind [lean-lang.org/eval](https://lean-lang.org/eval/)):
port the statement module to lean-eval's toolchain, tag the theorem
`@[eval_problem]`, add a `manifests/problems/<id>.toml` (`holes`, `submitter`,
`source`, `informal_solution`), and open a PR to lean-eval.  Large
self-contained statement preludes have precedent there (the knot-theory
problems ship a 23 KB trusted `ChallengeDeps.lean`).  Solvers edit only
`Submission.lean`; scoring is comparator acceptance, with submissions run by
the Lean FRO's hosted pipeline.

The challenge has exactly the four intended root theorem proof holes, imports only Mathlib and generated `Challenge.*` modules, and retains the direct raw effects.\n- Normal commit hooks passed 843 tests with 9 expected skips and all statement-integrity, proof-debt, conclusion-shaped-hypothesis, unfaithful-marker, and explicit-axiom audits.\n\nPending verification: final-head local CI and independent review; official comparator equality for all four closures, including private/compiler-generated completeness auxiliaries; real landrun with nanoda; and a verified merged-main library pin. This PR does not claim comparator acceptance.\n\n---\nAddresses #662\n",
