results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-pulls.json:398:  "body": "Addresses #652\n\n### Motivation\n\nThe comparator challenge generator under `scripts/comparator/` kept every\nchallenge's elaboration context in generator code: `challenges.py` held the\n`LDT_*` and `QPBT_*` `EXTRAS`/`MODULE_PRELUDES` pairs, the import block lived in\n`extract_closure.lean` and the target list was hard-coded next to it, so adding\nor changing a challenge meant editing Python and Lean sources that every other\nchallenge shares.\n\nThis PR moves the whole description of one challenge into one JSON file under\n`scripts/comparator/challenges/`, so a further challenge is added by adding a\nfile. It is tooling only: no Lean library module, no theorem statement, no\nblueprint file and no `docs/comparator.md` is touched, and the two challenges\nchecked in on `main` are reproduced byte for byte.\n\n### Description\n\n- `scripts/comparator/challenge_config.py` (new) \u2014 loads and validates one JSON\n  configuration per challenge: `imports`, `targets`, `header`, `footer`,\n  `expected`, `require_expected`, `extras`, `module_preludes`. Unknown top-level\n  and per-scope keys are rejected, so a typo fails loudly instead of silently\n  dropping elaboration context, and the scopes configured for one module are\n  checked for overlap. The schema, with the meaning of every key, is documented\n  at the top of the module.\n- `scripts/comparator/challenges.py` (deleted) \u2014 its two tables move verbatim\n  into the configuration files below.\n- `challenges/ldt.json` (new) \u2014 the LDT challenge: target\n  `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal`, expected copy\n  `expected/Challenge.lean.expected`, carrying `main`'s `LDT_EXTRAS` and\n  `LDT_MODULE_PRELUDES` key for key.\n- `challenges/qpbt.json` (new) \u2014 the Pauli basis test challenge: imports\n  `MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.Soundness` and `MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.QubitForm`, the two\n  targets `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` and\n  `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit`, the header/footer pair already on\n  `main`, expected copy `expected/ChallengeQPBT.lean.expected`, and\n  `require_expected: true` \u2014 the challenge is checked in, so its drift check\n  really runs. It carries `main`'s `QPBT_EXTRAS` and all fifteen\n  `QPBT_MODULE_PRELUDES` modules with the same namespaces, line ranges and\n  `noncomputable` flags.\n- `extract_closure.lean` \u2014 closes the statements of several targets, read from\n  `MIPSTARRE_COMPARATOR_TARGETS` and defaulting to the LDT main theorem so the\n  file still runs on its own as documented; a variable that is set but names no\n  target now fails loudly where the old code fell back silently. A Lean module\n  header cannot be computed at elaboration time, so a challenge's `imports` are\n  substituted into a rendered copy of the file.\n- `assemble_challenge.py` \u2014 the context tables come from the selected challenge\n  (`--challenge`, default `ldt`); the stale-table failure is scoped to that\n  challenge's own keys and names its configuration file.\n- `check_challenge_drift.py` \u2014 checks every configured challenge; renders the\n  extractor per challenge; `--challenge NAME` (repeatable) restricts the run and\n  `--write PATH` generates a challenge elsewhere while developing it. A\n  challenge whose expected copy is absent is an error under\n  `require_expected: true` and a reported skip otherwise, and `--update` refuses\n  a challenge whose configured header or footer file is not in the tree rather\n  than checking in a copy that omits that part.\n- `scripts/comparator/README.md` \u2014 the challenge table, a pointer to the\n  configuration schema, the new flags, and a manual regeneration pipeline that\n  now starts by rendering the extractor, so the block is runnable as shown for\n  QPBT as well as for LDT.\n- `scripts/tests/` \u2014 new `test_comparator_challenge_config.py` covering\n  configuration loading and rejection, multi-target ordering and its\n  independence from the extractor's row order, per-challenge stale-table\n  detection, the absent-expected-file case in both forms, and the `--update`\n  refusal; the assembler and drift tests are updated to the configuration API.\n\nThe CI drift step and `local/bin/ci.sh` are unchanged: with no `--challenge`\nthey now cover every configuration, so a further challenge is picked up by\nadding its file alone.\n\n### Testing\n\nIn a warm worktree of this branch, merged with `github/main`:\n\n- `python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root .`:\n  `challenge 'ldt' is current: scripts/comparator/expected/Challenge.lean.expected`\n  and\n  `challenge 'qpbt' is current: scripts/comparator/expected/ChallengeQPBT.lean.expected`\n  \u2014 both checked-in expected copies regenerate **byte-identically** through the\n  rendered extractor and the configuration-driven tables. That is the check that\n  the transcription out of `challenges.py` lost no elaboration context: a\n  dropped prelude changes the output and a stale key fails the assembler.\n- the manual pipeline documented in `README.md` run step by step for the QPBT\n  challenge (render the extractor, `lake env lean` with\n  `MIPSTARRE_COMPARATOR_TARGETS`, assemble, concatenate header and footer): the\n  result is byte-identical to the checked-in\n  `expected/ChallengeQPBT.lean.expected`.\n- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'` (the pre-commit\n  gate) green, with a clean `git status` afterwards.\n- repository CI on the pushed head.\n",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-pulls.json:761:  "body": "Addresses #637.\n\nCreates `docs/DEVIATIONS.md`, one reviewer-facing page listing every recorded place where the Lean development differs from the source paper (arXiv:2001.04383), and points the `texra-blueprint.toml` URLs at this repository. Only those two files change. Docs only; no Lean touched.\n\n## What the page contains\n\nEvery row gives: the paper statement and locator (`references/qpbt-paper/...`, chapter and lines), what differs, why in one or two plain sentences, the Lean carrier with `file:line`, the blueprint node and chapter file, the gap note, and a **printed-claim status** of `refuted` / `unproved` / `restated`.\n\nGrouped by severity:\n\n- **(a) Printed claims the source does not establish** \u2014 the two recorded as non-asserted `Prop`s. `PrintedExtendedLinesWitnessClaim` (`Combining/Apply.lean:108`), status *unproved*; `PrintedSymmetricProjectiveAttainmentClaim` (`Games/StrategyClasses.lean:901`), status *refuted*, with the refutation at `StrategyClasses.lean:952`.\n- **(b) Corrected constants and error forms** \u2014 7 rows: anticommuting probability, the `k <= m` exponent comparison, linearity `delta -> 2 delta`, the pasting product form, the binary factor index, the winning implications, the extraction triangle estimates.\n- **(c) Added side conditions and domain restrictions** \u2014 9 rows. The section opens by drawing the distinction `policy.tex` requires, between a boundary hypothesis (a faithful encoding of the source domain) and a hypothesis that supplies an unproved step; rows c1 (Magic Square rigidity) and c7 (the linearity zero-state-padding step) are marked as the latter.\n- **(d) Presentation-only** \u2014 2 rows: the field-valued combined-point construction (a change of proof, not of theorem) and the polynomial-error convention.\n\nAll 20 `qpbt_*.tex` notes are covered.\n\n## No headline theorem rests on an unproved claim\n\nStated explicitly, with three checks a reviewer can run, two mechanical and one manual:\n\n1. Both printed claims are `def ... : Prop`, which states a proposition without proving it. The comparator `git grep -n \"PrintedExtendedLinesWitnessClaim\\|PrintedSymmetricProjectiveAttainmentClaim\" -- \"MIPStarRE/**/*.lean\"` returns seven lines at `c6c8c2f2`: the two definitions, the refutation, and four docstring mentions. No theorem takes either as a hypothesis.\n2. No proof debt: every hit of `sorry`/`admit`/`native_decide`/`unsafe`/`implemented_by` in the Lean tree is inside prose, all of it in `LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean` and one `LDT` successor file recording that a former `sorryAx` dependency was removed. Zero real sites.\n3. `#print axioms pauli_soundness` must report exactly `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.\n\nCheck 3 is recorded with an honest caveat: the 2026-09-18 whole-environment sweep was run from a one-off metaprogram in a discarded worktree and **is not reproducible from this repository today** \u2014 there are zero `#print axioms` directives in the tree and the only committed audit module covers LDT, never QPBT. The page says a reviewer must run it by hand until a QPBT axiom-audit module lands.\n\nThe page also records what is genuinely open \u2014 the two source imports under issue #527, the tensor-code game correspondence and the `K >= 12 m (d + 1)` requirement \u2014 and says where they sit: they are obligations of the source's route to `lem:ld-soundness`, while the formalization reaches `exists_ld_soundness` by a different complete route, so they are not load-bearing for any headline theorem. A closing section records the `deltaQld` non-triviality question, which is adjacent rather than a deviation.\n\n## Where the register and the repository disagree\n\nChecked every row against `github/main` at `c6c8c2f2`. Two disagreements, reported here and **not** silently fixed in the register:\n\n1. **The register is missing two notes.** `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt-gap-register.md` has 18 rows, but 20 `qpbt_*.tex` notes exist on main. `qpbt_combined-points-field-valued.tex` (dated 2026-09-14) and `qpbt_subline-claims-line-marginal.tex` (2026-09-09) have no register row, although both are live: the first is cited from 7 Lean files, the second from 5 Lean files and from four sites in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex` (lines 2439, 3277, 3596, 3896). The register's own closing paragraph asks that a row be added whenever a note is added, so this looks like an oversight rather than a decision. Both are covered on the new page (d1 and c8). A follow-up should add the two rows.\n2. **An assertion in the register is not reproducible in-repo.** The register states that `exists_ld_soundness` \"is proved on main with the three standard axioms\". That is believed correct, but nothing in the repository checks it, for the reason given under check 3 above. The new page carries the caveat; the register does not.\n\nEverything else checked out. All 20 blueprint labels cited on the page resolve in `blueprint/src/chapter/`, and every Lean declaration cited was confirmed present at the stated file and line on `github/main`. In",

The original validation and costs below are historical claims;\n+this preservation does not independently revalidate them or reset any budget.\n+\n+# Direct-game error absorption: independent second attempt at issue #513\n+\n+## Result\n+\n+The statement and proof hole of `exists_globalPairWitness` are unchanged from\n+the pinned base `d647a4818ef43092aa66404834b99f2cb292ede8`. This attempt proves\n+two numerical prerequisites in `Combining/DirectPassingErrorBounds.lean`.\n+Neither theorem assumes a point witness, a line witness, or a global pair\n+witness. Their hypotheses concern only real functions and scalar constants.\n+\n+Let `p(epsilon)` be a polynomial point error and `f(epsilon,rho)` a polynomial\n+line error in the corrected additive sense of `IsPolyErr` and `IsPolyErr₂`.\n+For `c >= 0` and a real dimension `D >= 1`, the first theorem proves\n+\n+\\[\n+\\min\\{1,3(\\sqrt{p(\\epsilon)+cD f(\\epsilon,\\rho)}+\\rho)\\}\n+\\le D g(\\epsilon,\\rho)\n+\\]\n+\n+for a polynomial error function `g`, uniformly for nonnegative arguments.\n+The point error and the line error both occur under the square root.\n+The dimension factor is retained. The probability cap permits this statement\n+on the entire nonnegative quadrant even when the two errors have different\n+power bounds.\n+\n+For `rho = md/q`, put\n+\n+\\[\n+\\eta=3(\\sqrt{p(\\epsilon)+cmf(\\epsilon,\\rho)}+\\rho).\n+\\]\n+\n+The second theorem proves that, for fixed `a >= 1`, `0 < b <= 1`, and\n+`C >= 0`, there are universal `A > 1` and `0 < B < 1` such that\n+\n+\\[\n+\\min\\{1,C(\\delta_{\\rm ld}(a,b,\\eta+\\epsilon,q,2m+2,d,1)\n+  +\\sqrt{p(\\epsilon)}+\\rho)\\}\n+\\le A(md)^A(\\epsilon^B+q^{-B}+2^{-Bmd}).\n+\\]\n+\n+The constants are chosen before the admissible parameters and the test\n+error. The `deltaLd` input uses the full passing envelope, not its cap.\n+The proof first handles the cap using the first theorem and the existing\n+`exists_global_pair_error_bound`. If `eta > 1`, low-degree soundness at the\n+capped input `1 + epsilon` already has error at least one. Applying the\n+existing absorption with final scale `C + 1` then bounds the final cap in\n+the uncapped statement as well. The additive `epsilon` allows a positive\n+soundness input whenever the original test error is positive.\n+\n+## Source and reused content\n+\n+The source read before the proof was\n+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1267-1288`,\n+`lem:qld-4-7`, followed by its blueprint entry. The closing substitution was\n+checked at paper lines 1380-1404, especially `eq:qld-sgg-mhat-sandwich`.\n+The new bounds are separately labelled Lean-only scalar results:\n+`thm:qld-direct-passing-polynomial-bound` and\n+`thm:qld-direct-global-pair-error-bound`. The source theorem remains\n+`notready`.\n+\n+All saved Git refs were searched for the target and relevant error bounds.\n+The following existing work is distinguished from this attempt:\n+\n+- The first attempt's immutable checkpoint is the audit\n+  `2026-09-12_issue-513_pair-completion.md` at commit\n+  `dd9b0850380b32e7ec721e2bd4f7e1f8a42a572b`, PR #535. Its recovered\n+  completion constructions and new retained-overlap estimates are not copied\n+  or rederived here. That worktree was read only.\n+- `exists_global_pair_error_bound` was already present on main, with saved\n+  history `0f4ef053` and naming correction `fc18d3ab`. The new proof invokes\n+  it rather than repeating its real-power and dimension estimates.\n+- `directPassingErrorEnvelope`, from `2fe0b6b8`, and\n+  `ExtendedLineGame.strategy_value_ge_directPassingErrorEnvelope`, from\n+  `50ba6804`, are present at the pinned base. Their actual argument is\n+  `deltaQ + deltaL`, with collision contribution `md/q`. This is the\n+  expression treated by the new lemmas.\n+- Main's `exists_direct_ld_soundness` supplies the three directly indexed\n+  soundness bounds. Its public statement and axiom closure were checked.\n+- Saved commit `7b232dfa` includes\n+  `exists_direct_polynomial_measurements_of_supplied_witnesses`, originally\n+  `0ca9cfca`. Its statement takes both witnesses and returns POVMs on the\n+  original expanded spaces. It asserts neither projectivity nor existence\n+  of a polynomial-pair witness. It is not imported or used in this proof.\n+\n+## Remaining obligations\n+\n+The new result closes the numerical substitution for the actual direct-game\n+passing envelope. It does not prove that all measurements in the source\n+construction exist. In particular:\n+\n+1. The source strategy must produce the extended-line witness with the\n+   established line error. A helper that takes this witness is not its\n+   construction.\n+2. Direct soundness yields polynomial POVMs. The target requires projective\n+   polynomial-pair measurements on `S.ExpandedLocalSpace side`. Applying\n+   Naimark dilation changes the space, while compression of a projective\n+   measurement generally gives a POVM; the required projectivity and space\n+   must therefore be proved together.\n+3. The ordered correlations `eq:qld-g-42` and `eq:qld-g-43`, the concentration\n+   estimate `eq:qld-g-non-separable`, and the retained point-overlap bounds\n+   leading to `eq:qld-sgg-mhat-sandwich` remain necessary. They must preserve\n+   the soundness and point-error contributions and both heterogeneous\n+   placements. This packet assumes none of these operator inequalities.\n+4. The first attempt's completion bounds can be used only after those\n+   retained-overlap estimates are established. The scalar theorem here\n+   absorbs their displayed final error; it cannot supply the estimates.\n+\n+These are missing constructions, not a counterexample to the source theorem.\n+The separate defects in the printed seed-indexed soundness import remain\n+documented in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`. Using the\n+direct theorem does not certify that printed tensor-code reduction.\n+\n+## Statement-integrity audit\n+\n+- Paper assumptions: admissible parameters and a projective Pauli-basis\n+  strategy with value at least `1 - epsilon`, for positive `epsilon`.\n+- Lean assumptions: the same preexisting `AdmissibleParams`, positive error,\n+  and `ProjectiveSetting`. The target acquires no new input.\n+- Paper conclusion: constants `a > 1`, `0 < b < 1`, chosen universally,\n+  and projective measurements of global polynomial pairs on both expanded\n+  local spaces, consistent with the opposite point measurements for each\n+  Pauli basis, with the specified error function.\n+- Lean conclusion: unchanged `GlobalPairWitness` and `deltaQld`, with the\n+  same quantifier order, constants, and four consistency requirements.\n+- Verdict: target statement preserved with its existing finite-space\n+  encoding; proof incomplete. The new scalar statements are independent\n+  auxiliary estimates and are not replacements for the source theorem.\n+\n+## Validation\n+\n+- Focused Lean checks of the new module and `Apply.lean` pass. All except the target\n+  use only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. The source theorem's completion status\n+  is unchanged.\n+- Hook installation and whitespace checks pass. Exact-head CI and PR\n+  publication are reported in the PR and final session handoff, not assumed\n+  by this checkpoint.\n+\n+## Cost accounting\n+\n+The three earlier #119 prover sessions recorded in the first checkpoint have\n+1927 seconds of total session span, 18,472,194 input tokens, 18,088,320 cached\n+input tokens, and 56,839 output tokens (including 17,733 reasoning tokens).\n+The two later #119 scout records have unknown active-time attribution and\n+nonadditive token snapshots; they remain excluded from these sums, not\n+erased from the history.\n+\n+The completed dispatcher receipt for `prover-513-20260912-01` records\n+`2026-09-12T04:56:37Z` through `2026-09-12T05:56:39Z`, 3602 seconds,\n+13,083,296 input tokens, 12,717,696 cached input tokens, and 30,819 output\n+tokens (including 10,671 reasoning tokens). Thus the additive recorded\n+predecessor totals are 5529 session-seconds, 31,555,490 input tokens,\n+30,806,016 cached input tokens, and 87,658 output tokens, including 28,404\n+reasoning tokens. Cached input is part of input and reasoning is part of\n+output; neither is added a second time. Session span is not a measurement\n+of active proof time.\n+\n+This second attempt is separately dispatched as `prover-513-20260912-02`,\n+starting at `2026-09-12T05:41:53Z`, with a 60-active-minute bound and no\n+descendants. Its final usage belongs to its own dispatcher receipt. The\n+overlap in calendar time with the first attempt does not reset either\n+budget or make their token totals nonadditive. results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:316:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: opus-bc57dd05-comparator-acceptance -->\nThe official Lean comparator (`leanprover/comparator`, pinned at v4.32.0) was run\nfor the first time end to end against the QPBT challenge on 2026-09-19\n(report `/tmp/meta-qpbt-comparator-verify-20260919.md`, packet K5).  The build,\nthe axiom criterion and a full `lean4checker` kernel replay of all 675 modules\nall pass, but the comparator **rejects** the pair:\n\n\u200b`\u200b`\u200b`\nuncaught exception: Const does not match between challenge and target\n                    'MIPStarRE.QPBT.qubitOperatorDistanceB'\n\u200b`\u200b`\u200b`\n\n## Cause\n\n`MIPStarRE.QPBT.QubitRegister P` unfolds to\n`Cube P.m \u00d7 Fin P.model.basisDim \u2192 ZMod 2`, so giving it a `Fintype` needs\n`@ZMod.fintype 2 _`, whose `NeZero` argument is a *proof*.  Lean abstracts a\nnon-trivial nested proof out of a definition's value into an auto-generated\nauxiliary constant, and names that constant after whichever declaration first\nneeded it.  That declaration is not the same in the two environments:\n\n| environment | auxiliary constant | statement | value |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| library (`Solution`) | `MIPStarRE.QPBT.idealQubitState._proof_2` | `NeZero (1 + 1)` | `@Nat.instNeZeroSucc 1` |\n| Mathlib-only `Challenge` | `MIPStarRE.QPBT.qubitPauliProj._proof_1` | `NeZero (1 + 1)` | `@Nat.instNeZeroSucc 1` |\n\nSame proposition, same proof term, different *name* \u2014 so\n`qubitOperatorDistanceA` and `qubitOperatorDistanceB` differ structurally and\nthe comparator stops at the first one it reaches.  This is not a soundness\nproblem; the kernel replay passes.\n\n## Work\n\nName every order-dependent auxiliary constant that appears in the QPBT\nstatement closure, so no `_proof_N` constant whose name depends on elaboration\norder survives in it.  This is the same class of repair as\n`fix(qpbt): name the Galois local instances in the closure`.\n\nAll changes must be statement-preserving: the statements of\n`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` and\n`MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one` stay byte-identical, no `sorry`, no new\naxiom, standard axioms only.\n\n## Acceptance\n\nA local comparator run in `/home/drx/QPBT-comparator` (branch `draft-challenge`,\n`./verify.sh --fake-landrun`) accepts the challenge/solution pair.",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:550:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: comparator-challenge-for-the-qpbt-headline-theorems-tooling-7e17e7e2 -->\nThe LDT headline theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` is already covered by\na comparator challenge (`docs/comparator.md`, `scripts/comparator/`, companion\nrepository `LDT-comparator`).  The QPBT headline theorems have no such\ncoverage.\n\nThis issue tracks giving `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` and\n`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` the same treatment:\n\n1. **Tooling parameterization.**  `scripts/comparator/` is currently\n   single-challenge: the extractor hard-codes the LDT root, and the assembler's\n   elaboration-context tables are LDT-specific.  Introduce a per-challenge\n   configuration (target theorem names, header, footer, expected file path,\n   context tables) without changing the LDT outputs by a single byte \u2014\n   `check_challenge_drift.py` must still pass for LDT.\n2. **Closure extraction.**  Produce\n   `scripts/comparator/expected/ChallengeQPBT.lean.expected`: a Mathlib-only\n   file that re-declares every declaration of the comparator-relevant statement\n   closure of the two QPBT targets verbatim and in dependency order, then states\n   both theorems with `sorry`.\n3. **Environment alignment.**  Every module contributing a declaration to the\n   QPBT closure must see the full `import Mathlib` (directly or through an\n   existing base module), carrying the same \"do not narrow this import\"\n   comment, so the challenge file elaborates to terms identical to the\n   library's.  Verbatim-redeclaration obstacles (custom notation, local\n   instances, private or auxiliary declarations, `open ... in`, attribute side\n   effects) are resolved with the smallest faithful edits \u2014 no statement and no\n   proof term of a headline theorem changes.\n4. **Documentation and CI.**  A QPBT section in `docs/comparator.md` and a QPBT\n   drift check next to the LDT one in `pr-ci.yml`.\n\nThe challenge repository itself is\n<https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator>; its `draft-challenge` branch\nreceives `Challenge.lean`, `Solution.lean`, `lakefile.toml`, `comparator.json`\nand `verify.sh`, with the library pinned by commit.\n\nConstraints: no `sorry`/`admit`/`axiom` enters the library, the statements of\n`pauli_soundness` and `pauli_soundness_qubit` stay byte-identical, and the\naxiom closure stays `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.",

Requested\n  CLI Ultra is distinct from wire/returned Max seen in owner migration receipts;\n  absent request-specific wire evidence stays null, not inferred from configuration.\n- **Every full build** (warmer, CI, cold rebuild) lands in `builds.jsonl`.\n- **Stage transitions** are logged by the orchestrator (main session) at the\n  moment they happen, not reconstructed later.\n- Claude-side (non-Codex) subagent fleets are recorded in\n  `owner-sessions.jsonl` and summarized into `stages.jsonl` as `milestone`\n  entries with token totals, since they bypass `dispatch.sh`.\n\n## Research-data invariants\n\nModel-policy records (#301) retain `requested_model`, `selected_model`,\n`effective_model` only when observed, `job_class`, and `model_policy` with\nroutine/hard classification and the explicit hardness/escalation rationale.\nExternal capture without model evidence records effective model as null, not the\nCLI argument. Historical native observations retain all bound current-turn contexts; mixed\nmodels/efforts and requested/observed mismatches fail closed. Prior/forked contexts\nare not attributed to a new job. Requested effort remains distinct from provider\neffort; missing usage remains unknown and historical records are not rewritten.\n`dispatch_kind` is new/resume/grandfathered; `activation_at` fixes the accounting\nboundary. Ratio reports count actual distinct new threads with matching observed\nand selected models, with a rolling 100-dispatch window and separate cumulative\ncounts. Unknowns may resolve from later observations; conflicts remain unknown.\nMain, pre-activation workers and resumes do not count. Preserve predecessor and\ncumulative-budget links recorded when a model change required a fresh native identity.\n\nThe project doubles as a study of a self-evolving formalization workflow.\nThree artifacts must therefore stay trustworthy:\n\n- `EVOLUTION.md` — complete: every protocol change has an entry.\n- `events.md` — honest: failures are recorded as failures, including agent\n  mistakes, wasted builds, and reverted work.\n- `sessions.jsonl` + `stages.jsonl` — quantitative: per-stage cost\n  (time, tokens, session counts) reconstructible by a script, not by memory.\n# Build cache protocol — the hot main cache\n\nNormative. This document specifies the local replacement for the parent\nworkflow's GitHub Actions build cache, and the rules every worktree must obey to\navoid duplicate compilation. It is the protocol behind three executables:\n\n| script | role |\n|---|---|\n| `local/bin/cache-warmer.sh` | the **single writer**: builds `main`, publishes read-only snapshots |\n| `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh` | the **consumer**: keyhash-gated copy-on-write clone into a worktree |\n| `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` | fresh-worktree bootstrap (replaces `.codex/setup.sh`) |\n\nGoverning invariants: `local/DESIGN.md` #1 (single cache writer) and #7 (one full\n`lake build` machine-wide). Where this document and `DESIGN.md` disagree,\n`DESIGN.md` wins.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What is being replaced, and why it was built that way\n\nThe parent repository's caching design is the residue of a specific, documented\nfailure. The load-bearing citations:\n\n| parent mechanism | citation | what it encodes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Split restore/save, save only on `main` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:137-167` | *\"The cache is saved only from main and restored everywhere.\"* |\n| `lean-action`'s own cache disabled | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:138-142` | The post-mortem: a ~2.6 GB entry saved **per PR run** cycled through the 10 GB repository cache budget and evicted the main-branch entry, *\"so no run ever restored usable MIPStarRE oleans and every run rebuilt the whole library.\"* |\n| Same policy restated in the weekly job | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:75-77` | *\"See pr-ci.yml: per-run lake caches evict the main build cache from the repository cache budget.\"* |\n| Main runs exempt from cancellation | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:50` | *\"Do not cancel main-branch runs: they seed the build cache.\"* |\n| Save runs `if: always()` on main | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:161-162` | *\"Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still spares the next run the modules that did compile.\"* |\n| ProofWidgets prune workaround | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:56-69` | A fresh-tree upstream bug that aborts the entire Mathlib cache fetch |\n| `elan` install isolated from the cache lifecycle | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:44-54` | Avoids *\"a partial cache save or restore-then-overwrite that could are manual only | `.github/workflows/update.yml:3-5` | A bump *\"triggers a full library rebuild and possibly an auto-fix cascade\"* |\n| Lean setup removed from a PR job | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:314` | A job was demoted to a notice *\"after repeated runner disk exhaustion\"* |\n\nThe single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable\ncache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the\nsame failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared\nbuild tree.\n\n---\n\n## 2. The two-tier split\n\n`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and\ndifferent sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the\nparent's failure.\n\nAn absolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` relocates `.lake` to `<root>/<branch>` for a\none-component branch name. The helper rejects `/`, symlink targets, escape, and\ncanonical overlap with packages, `hot-main`, the repository, or any worktree,\nplus canonical-equal ownership by another worktree. Export it before setup or\nwarming and through dispatch and cleanup; only its target gets `--add-dir`.\n\n**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,\n`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the\nparent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and\ndistributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**\ncopy.\n\n**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The\nparent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud\ncache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally they live **once\nper manifest** in a shared, read-only store:\n`$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`, `key = sha256(lake-manifest.json ‖ lean-toolchain)[:16]`,\nand every worktree's `.lake/packages` is a symlink to it.\n\n> **Why a shared store is safe here (2026-09-03).** The old objection — a\n> shared tree is read-only only by convention, so one `lake update` mutates it\n> for everyone — is answered mechanically: the store is `chmod -R a-w`, so any\n> write (an automated `lake update`, a dependency rebuild after a manifest\n> drift) fails loudly in the one worktree that attempted it. Identity is by\n> key, so a Mathlib bump simply creates a new store entry; worktrees on the old\n> manifest keep linking the old one. The first worktree to need a key fetches\n> with `lake exe cache get` into a real directory, then *publishes* it (move,\n> `chmod a-w`, link); later worktrees only link. Cost: 7.3 GB once per key\n> instead of per worktree (8 copies = 58 GB on 2026-09-03, on a 97 % full disk).\n> `worktree-setup.sh` still refuses to run `lake update`.\n\nConsequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It\nrewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under\nevery published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib\nbumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.\n\n---\n\n## 3. The cache key\n\n```\nkeyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )\n```\n\nconcatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local\nanalog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in\n`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`\nand `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay\nbyte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.\nA missing input file is a hard error, never a default.\n\nTwo properties matter, and they are not symmetric:\n\n1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's\n   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest\n   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is\n   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash\n   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not\n   need their timestamps preserved.\n2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,\n   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.\n   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`\n   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls\n   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.\n\n---\n\n## 4. On-disk layout\n\nShared packages and `hot-main` use `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`; branch products may\nuse `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` as in §2. Neither runtime tree is committed.\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/\n├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time\n│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose\n├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends\n├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)\n└── hot-main/\n    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this\n    │   └── info\n    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main\n    ├── snapshots/\n    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    │   │   ├── STAMP\n    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build\n    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink\n```\n\nSnapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse\nlexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`\ncalls and no name parsing.\n\n### `STAMP` schema\n\nA flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts\nparse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase\nhex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever\n`eval`ed or `source`d.\n\n```\nsha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>\nkeyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>\ntimestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>\ntimestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>\nstatus=complete|partial\nbuild_seconds=<integer>\ntoolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>\nsnapshot=<snapshot directory name>\nwarmer_version=1\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]\n                          [--targets \"<lake targets>\"] [--lock-timeout S]\n                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]\n```\n\n### 5.1 Writer lease\n\nAcquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic\ntest-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,\n`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.\n\nStaleness is decided in this order:\n\n* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead\n  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.\n* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).\n\nThe TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this\nrepository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,\n2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease\nmid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to\nprevent.\n\n**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that\nboth judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;\n`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and\nre-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A\n`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.\n\n### 5.2 Build\n\n1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`\n   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.\n   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and\n   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).\n2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).\n3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**\n   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and\n   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,\n   finish, then warm again.\n4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply\n   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.\n   **No `lake update`.**\n5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.\n   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is\n   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent\n   prompts may later read.\n\n### 5.3 Atomic publish\n\nThe publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:\n\n1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with\n   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the\n   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).\n2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.\n3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.\n   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already\n   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**\n4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over\n   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).\n\n> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,\n> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would\n> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real\n> trap, not a hypothetical one.\n\nConsumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the\nresolved concrete path for the rest of the run.\n\n### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional\n\nIf `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and\nexits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`\ncommit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did\ncompile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say\nso loudly.\n\nA non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *\"main did not build cleanly\"* —\nnot *\"nothing was published.\"* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a\nreason to retry.\n\n### 5.5 Retention\n\nKeep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's\n10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never\ncollected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has\nresolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging\ndirectories older than an hour are swept.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]\n                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]\n```\n\nThe consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to\noperate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.\n\nDecision procedure:\n\n1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).\n2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.\n3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. A malformed stamp is treated as *no snapshot*.\n4. **Keyhash gate.** Mismatch → warn with both hashes, name the likely cause\n   (toolchain / manifest / lakefile change), point at the warmer, and take the\n   cold path. Never a partial reuse, never a silent skip.\n5. **Warm path**: `cp -c -R <snapshot>/build → <worktree>/.lake/build.incoming.$$`,\n   then `rename` into place. Write the idempotency marker\n   `<worktree>/.lake/.mipstarre-warm-stamp` recording the snapshot name, keyhash,\n   snapshot status and time. Then fetch tier 2 with `lake exe cache get`.\n   No full build unless `--build` is given — the point of the warm path is that\n   the agent's next incremental `lake build` compiles only its own delta.\n6. **Cold path**: `lake exe cache get`, then a full `lake build` under the\n   machine-wide lock (§7), unless `--no-build`.\n\n### 6.1 Idempotency and the do-not-clobber rule\n\nRe-running on an already-warmed worktree is a no-op for tier 1. Specifically:\n\n* marker snapshot **and** keyhash both match the resolved snapshot → skip the\n  clone;\n* `.lake/build` is populated but was **not** warmed from this snapshot → leave it\n  alone and warn. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it\n  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.\n\n### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink\n\nOn APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near\ninstantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid\nfor only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. This is what makes a\n*private writable copy per worktree* affordable — and a private writable copy is\nprecisely what preserves the single-writer invariant. A writable symlink or\nbind-style share of `.lake/build` across two concurrent `lake build` invocations\nis the local restatement of the parent's eviction bug and is never acceptable.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Concurrency: two locks, deliberately separate\n\n| lock | path | held by | protects |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| writer lease | `hot-main/.writer-lease` | the warmer only | the snapshot store and `hot-main/repo` |\n| full-build lock | `.full-build-lock` | warmer **and** consumers | RAM/CPU: one full `lake build` machine-wide |\n\nThey are separate so that a consumer's own full build can proceed while the\nwarmer sits idle between commits, and so that a warmer holding the writer lease\ndoes not block a consumer that only wants to *read* a published snapshot.\n\n`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They\nare read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`\ngate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add\nlocking there.\n\nThe parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that\na CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice\n(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale\nbuild; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.\n\nBoth locks use the same mkdir/rename-to-break protocol described in §5.1, with\nthe same liveness-first staleness rule, so a consumer and the warmer agree on\nwhat a stale lock is.\n\n### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`\n\n`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two\ncompatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:\n\n* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,\n  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to\n  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override\n  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the\n  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the\n  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,\n  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see\n  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)\n* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO\n  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.\n  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude \"no pid, therefore\n  stale\" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here\n  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then\n  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`\n  field is read as \"this host\", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`\n\nReplaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s\nGitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:\n\n1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a\n   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable\n   error.\n2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is\n   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.\n3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only\n   if the pin is not already installed.\n4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).\n5. **`origin/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a warning, because the hooks and every\n   diff-based audit silently self-disable without it. Silent self-disabling is the\n   documented failure this check exists to surface.\n6. **Fresh-state workaround** (§8.2).\n7. **`warm-worktree.sh`** — invoked from the copy *next to this script*, not the\n   copy inside the worktree being bootstrapped. A worktree may hold an unreviewed\n   branch; the bootstrap must not execute code from the tree it is bootstrapping.\n   This is the local analog of `DESIGN.md` #5 (trusted prompts come from `main`).\n   If the consumer script is missing, this is a **hard error**: without it the\n   worktree would start cold, silently, which is the outcome the whole protocol\n   exists to prevent.\n8. **`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`**, then `--check`. `docs/ci-automation.md`\n   calls out `--check` specifically for *\"each fresh worktree used for a PR.\"*\n\n`--check` is report-only and mutates nothing (`DESIGN.md` #10). It exits non-zero\nif anything is missing.\n\n### 8.1 Git environment hygiene\n\nEvery invocation of `lake` or of `git` inside a vendored package is wrapped in\n`run_outside_git_env`, ported from `.githooks/pre-push:19-25`: it unsets every\nvariable named by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` in a subshell. Without it, a\nscript invoked from inside a git hook leaks `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` into\nLake's package checkouts, and nested git operations resolve the wrong repository.\n\n### 8.2 The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround\n\nKept verbatim in intent from `docgen.yml:56-69`, in all three scripts, because a\npristine agent worktree is exactly the fresh state that triggers it.\n\n*Upstream form.* `lake exe cache get` runs `lake update`, whose mathlib\npost-update hook prunes `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib` before\nfetching a cloud release. On a tree that has never built, the directory does not\nexist, and the uncaught exception aborts the **entire** cache fetch. Fix: create\nthe directory, but only if `proofwidgets` was actually checked out.\n\n*Local form.* The same fetch also aborts when a vendored package tree is\n**dirty**: build byproducts (`widget/js/lake.trace`) block the revision checkout.\nRecorded in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, 2026-08-30 — a failed build followed\nby a successful retry after `git reset --hard` in the package. The scripts\ntherefore reset any vendored package tree with **tracked** modifications before\nfetching.\n\n`git clean` is deliberately **not** run inside a vendored package: it would delete\ndownloaded build output at a cost of hours. If an untracked byproduct still blocks\na checkout, the fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from\nsource.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Telemetry\n\nEvery full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.\n\n```jsonc\n{\"ts\": \"<ISO 8601 with offset>\",\n \"kind\": \"warm\" | \"rebuild\" | \"cache-get\",\n \"trigger\": \"<who asked for this>\",\n \"outcome\": \"success\" | \"failed\",\n \"seconds\": <int>,\n \"sha\": \"<commit, when known>\",\n \"note\": \"<sanitized, ≤400 chars>\"}\n```\n\n* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.\n* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).\n* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.\n\nThree properties are load-bearing:\n\n* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked\n  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the\n  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and\n  produce merge conflicts. Override with `MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR`.\n* **Appends are serialized** by a short-lived `mkdir` lock, and give up after 5 s\n  rather than delaying a build. Telemetry never blocks or fails a build; every\n  failure path degrades to a warning.\n* **`note` is sanitized** — non-printable characters stripped, truncated to 400\n  characters — because notes may quote build output, and compiler output is\n  untrusted text regardless of where it was produced (`DESIGN.md` #6).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Operating procedures\n\n```bash\n# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main\n\n# What is published right now?\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status\n\n# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/.worktrees/issue-0042-qpbt-basis\n\n# Verify an existing worktree without touching it.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check\n\n# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force\n\n# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status\n```\n\nAfter a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm\nfirst, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot\nis invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Failure modes and how each degrades\n\n| condition | behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |\n| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |\n| Malformed / unreadable `STAMP` | Treated as *no snapshot*; cold path. |\n| Snapshot is `partial` | Used, with a warning naming the SHA that failed. |\n| `cp -c` unsupported (non-APFS, cross-volume) | Warn, fall back to `cp -R`. Non-fatal. |\n| Full-build lock held | Wait; the warmer waits indefinitely by default, consumers time out per `--lock-timeout`. |\n| Stale lock (dead pid, or age > TTL) | Broken by atomic rename, with a warning naming the dead holder. |\n| Primary repo has no commits on `main` | Hard error naming the cause. Evidence contracts\n\nAll evidence binds to the **exact head SHA** (DESIGN.md invariant 2).\n\n**Commit statuses.** Ten canonical contexts, posted by `post-status`: one\n`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,\n`blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`,\n`statement-origin`), plus `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`.\n`ci.sh` posts `pending` before each gate step and `success | failure | error`\nafter it; a gated-out step is a `success` saying it was skipped. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`\ntoo — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review\nevent carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`\n(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.\n\n**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with\n`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition\nline per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.\n\n**Idempotency.** Every publishing step is **at most one mutation**: a paginated\nread finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating\nit (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than\nwebhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.\n\n## 3. The merge gate\n\n`pr_merge.py <number>` is the only path to `main`: never `git merge` to main,\nnever push `main`. After\n   fetching the current GitHub base, the head is fresh when that base is its\n   ancestor, or when every raw tree change from their merge base to the base is\n   allowlisted passive telemetry: a regular non-executable (`100644`) `.md` or\n   `.jsonl` file below `results/telemetry/`, or a generated regular\n   non-executable `.json` file below the exact\n   `results/telemetry/github-snapshot/` subtree. ## The QPBT challenge

The QPBT challenge is prepared for the separate repository
**[QPBT-comparator](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator)**.  Its current
configuration supplies these four theorem names to one comparator run:

- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one` (`lem:pauli-completeness`);
- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness` (`lem:ld-soundness`);
- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` (`thm:pauli`); and
- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` (`cor:pauli-binary`).

The checked-in generated tree is `scripts/comparator/expected/qpbt/`.  It has a
root `Challenge.lean` and thirty Mathlib-only mirror modules under `Challenge/`,
one for each contributing library module.  The root states all four targets
with `sorry`; the drift guard regenerates and byte-compares the complete tree
with `--challenge qpbt`.

### Current verification status

At library commit `a534c7f97ba34fd561ae03134f90b81ee4e395c1`, generation and
elaboration of this four-target tree passed, as did the canonical local CI
contexts.  Those checks establish that the generated challenge and library
compile.  They do **not** establish equality of every declaration in the union
of the four statement closures.  In particular, equality of the generated
private auxiliaries reached through the completeness target remains
unestablished.

The following checks are still pending for the four-target configuration:

- an official comparator run establishing all-four closure equality;
- equality of the private and compiler-generated completeness auxiliaries;
- real-landrun verification with nanoda enabled; and
- a challenge-repository pin to the verified commit after it reaches `main`.

There is a narrower historical result.  At commit
`4aec9ebedf6ca401e3f2d7b4bd90bd565d38f90d`, the split challenge configured
only `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` and
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit`.  On that exact two-target configuration,
`./verify.sh --fake-landrun` reported acceptance.  Fake landrun disables nanoda,
and that run did not include `exists_spcc_value_one` or `exists_ld_soundness`, so
it is not evidence for the current four-target challenge.

### Environment alignment for QPBT

Comparator compares the full kernel closure constant by constant, so each
Mathlib-only challenge module must elaborate to bit-identical terms.  The
library and generator use the following alignment measures:

1. **Full Mathlib imports.**  Four closure modules -
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Subspaces.lean`,
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Coefficients.lean`,
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/LowDegreeCode.lean`, and
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Lines.lean` - use the full `import Mathlib`, so tactic
   elaboration sees the same environment as the challenge modules.  Other
   closure modules receive Mathlib through existing shared imports.
2. **Public closure members.**  A `private` declaration's real name is qualified
   by its defining module (`_private.<module>.0.<name>`), so a challenge module
   cannot re-declare it under the library's name.  Closure members needed by the
   challenge were therefore made public without changing their statements,
   bodies, or proof scripts.
3. **Named local instances.**  The group and decidable-equality instances for
   the Galois group in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/FieldBasis.lean` have explicit
   names.  This avoids generated names that encode the defining module.
4. **Mirrored module partition.**  Lean caches nested proof and `match`
   auxiliaries per module, names them after the first declaration in that module
   that needs them, and limits instance synthesis to the module's imports.  The
   QPBT challenge therefore mirrors the source module partition and import
   graph.  This behavior is selected by `"split": true` in
   `scripts/comparator/challenges/qpbt.json`; `assemble_challenge.py --split-dir`
   writes the tree under `scripts/comparator/expected/qpbt/`.

The split layout also avoids adding QPBT-specific global instance wrappers to
`MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`.  The original LDT challenge bytes
are protected independently by the baseline regression described in
`scripts/comparator/README.md`.

No public statement of any of the four targets changed as part of this
comparator alignment.  Comparator equality remains pending as described above.

The "do not narrow this import" notes on the shared base modules
(`MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersBase.lean`,
`MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/Distribution.lean`,
`MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`) still name only `mainFormal`,
and deliberately so: those modules contribute to both closures, and adding a
line to a module docstring shifts every declaration below it, which would
rewrite the `-- source:` provenance comments of the checked-in LDT challenge.
They are covered by this section instead.

# Challenge: headline theorems of the quantum Pauli basis test

Self-contained comparator challenge for the four registered QPBT headline
theorems: low-degree soundness, completeness of the Pauli basis test, its
soundness theorem, and the qubit-coordinate soundness corollary.

The challenge is **Mathlib-only**: apart from Mathlib it imports nothing but
its own modules under `Challenge/`, one for each library module that
contributes to the closure.  Together they re-declare, verbatim and in
dependency order, every definition in the transitive closure of the statements
of the four theorems; the theorems themselves are stated here with `sorry`.
Those modules and their imports mirror the library's own module partition
and import graph.  That is not cosmetic: Lean caches a nested proof and
a `match` auxiliary *per module*, names it after the first declaration of that
module that needs it, and lets a declaration see only the instances its
module's imports bring into scope, while the comparator compares the full
`ConstantInfo` of every closure constant, values and proofs included.  A
single-file challenge therefore cannot reproduce those names whenever the
library needs the same fact in two modules; the mirrored partition reproduces
them by construction.

The set of challenge modules is the entire human audit surface: a reader who
agrees that they state the intended theorems does not need to read anything
else.  The
[comparator](https://github.com/leanprover/comparator) tool verifies
mechanically that the [MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE)
library declares statements identical to these and proves the theorems using
no axioms beyond `propext`, `Quot.sound`, and `Classical.choice`.

Each declaration carries a provenance comment (`-- source: <file>:<lines>`)
pointing at its origin in the MIPStarRE library, where docstrings cite the
paper passages being encoded, and each challenge module names the library
module it mirrors.  These files are generated by
`scripts/comparator/` in that repository; see the README alongside this file

-- source: MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean:82-108
--   (MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness)
/-- Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree test.
Blueprint `lem:ld-soundness`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`. -/
theorem exists_ld_soundness :
    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
      ∀ (L : LdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
        ∀ S : Strategy (ldGame L), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
          ∃ GA : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιA, ∃ GB : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιB,
            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
                (fun u outcome =>
                  heteroKron
                    (((S.A (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome) 1)
                (fun u outcome =>
                  heteroKron 1
                    ((GB.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
                (fun u outcome =>
                  heteroKron
                    ((GA.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
                (fun u outcome =>
                  heteroKron 1
                    (((S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome))
                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k := by
  sorry

# Comparator challenge generation

This directory generates the self-contained statement files `Challenge.lean`
used by companion repositories — for the low individual degree test,
[LDT-comparator](https://github.com/LionSR/LDT-comparator), and for the quantum
Pauli basis test,
[QPBT-comparator](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator) — to verify,
with the official
[leanprover/comparator](https://github.com/leanprover/comparator), that this
library proves the target theorems.  Background and trust model:
`docs/comparator.md`.

A generated challenge imports only Mathlib and, when split, its own mirror
modules.  It re-declares, verbatim and in dependency order, every declaration
in the kernel closure of its target statements, each with a provenance comment;
the targets themselves are stated with `sorry`.

## Challenges

Each challenge is one configuration file under `challenges/`:

| file | targets | expected copy | challenge repository |
|---|---|---|---|
| `challenges/ldt.json` | `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` | `expected/Challenge.lean.expected` | [LDT-comparator](https://github.com/LionSR/LDT-comparator) |
| `challenges/qpbt.json` | four QPBT headline theorems | `expected/qpbt/` (one module per library module) | [QPBT-comparator](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator) |

The four QPBT targets are `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one`,
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness`, and
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit`.

A configuration names the Lean modules the extractor imports, the target
theorems whose statement closure it takes, the header and footer files wrapped
around the assembled body, the checked-in expected copy, and the per-challenge
elaboration-context tables (`extras`, `module_preludes`).  The schema, with the
meaning of every key, is documented at the top of `challenge_config.py`; unknown
keys are rejected, so a typo fails loudly rather than silently dropping context.

`require_expected` distinguishes a challenge that must stay regenerated (`true`,
a missing expected copy is an error) from one still being developed (`false`,
a missing expected copy is reported and skipped).

Adding a challenge means adding a configuration file, a header and a footer —
no generator code changes and, for the machine-wide guard in `local/bin/ci.sh`,
no CI change either, because that guard passes no `--challenge` and therefore
checks every configuration it finds.

## Drift guard and regeneration

The repository keeps each generated challenge checked in under `expected/`.
The LDT copy has a final `.expected` suffix, which keeps that intentionally
monolithic fixture out of the 1000-line project-source guard; the QPBT copy is
a split directory. The PR CI guard regenerates every configured challenge in a
temporary directory and byte-compares it with the checked-in file or tree; it
never writes `Challenge.lean` at the repository root.

Run the deterministic guard from the repository root (requires a built
library).  With no `--challenge` every configured challenge is checked:

```sh
python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root .
python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root . --challenge qpbt
```

Add `--challenge <name>` (repeatable) to restrict the run to one challenge.

To update a checked-in expected copy after an intentional statement or
dependency change, run the exact maintenance command:

```sh
python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root . --update
```

That command refuses a challenge whose configured header or footer file is not
in the tree, and reports it as an error while still updating the others: the
copy it would write omits those statements, and once such a copy exists the
`require_expected: false` skip no longer applies, so every later drift run
would report a challenge that states nothing as current.

The regeneration guard and the LDT preservation regression answer different
questions.  Regeneration checks that the fixture agrees with the current
library.  `ComparatorChallengeDriftTests.test_ldt_expected_matches_original_baseline`
also hashes `expected/Challenge.lean.expected` and requires the original LDT
digest
`cbe5642bb88db75f86bd79936896e684aa407a02108d8259ead71a0738783e73`.
Consequently, a QPBT-only change cannot silently update both the library and the
generated LDT fixture.

For an intentional future LDT change, first regenerate from fresh built
metadata, audit the exact fixture diff, and verify it in LDT-comparator.  Then
update `LDT_BASELINE_SHA256` in
`scripts/tests/test_comparator_challenge_drift.py` explicitly in the same
reviewed change, with the mathematical reason for changing the LDT closure.

To generate a challenge somewhere else without touching the checked-in copy —
the usual loop while filling in a new challenge's context tables:

```sh
python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root . \
    --challenge qpbt --write /tmp/Challenge.lean
```

The update command performs the extraction and assembly pipeline below in a
temporary directory; the same steps run by hand, shown here for the QPBT
challenge, reproduce the same file:

```sh
# 1. render the extractor with this challenge's own import block.  A Lean module
#    header cannot be computed at elaboration time, so the checked-in
#    extract_closure.lean carries the LDT import block and every consumer
#    substitutes the challenge's `imports` into a copy of it; run unrendered on
#    a QPBT target it fails with "target not found", because no LDT module
#    imports QPBT.
python3 - <<'PY' > extract_closure_qpbt.lean
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts/comparator")
from challenge_config import load_challenges
from check_challenge_drift import EXTRACTOR, render_extractor
(challenge,) = load_challenges(["qpbt"])
sys.stdout.write(render_extractor(challenge, EXTRACTOR.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
PY

# 2. extract the closure of the challenge's target statements (a Lean
#    metaprogram mirroring comparator's runForUsedConsts traversal).  The
#    targets reach the extractor in MIPSTARRE_COMPARATOR_TARGETS; with that
#    variable unset it closes the LDT main theorem:
MIPSTARRE_COMPARATOR_TARGETS="MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness,MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit,MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one,MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness" \
  lake env lean extract_closure_qpbt.lean > closure.tsv
awk -F'\t' 'NF==4' closure.tsv > closure.clean.tsv

# 3. assemble the challenge body (topological order, namespace handling)
# `qpbt` is split, so the assembler writes a directory:
python3 scripts/comparator/assemble_challenge.py closure.clean.tsv \
    --challenge qpbt --split-dir scripts/comparator/expected/qpbt
```

For the LDT challenge step 1 is a no-op — the checked-in extractor already
carries that challenge's import block — so `lake env lean
scripts/comparator/extract_closure.lean` with no environment variable set is
step 2 of the LDT pipeline as it stands.

Then copy the expected file, or the QPBT `Challenge.lean` and `Challenge/`
tree, into the matching comparator repository. Bump the `rev` pin in its
`lakefile.toml` and `lake-manifest.json` to the library commit from which it was
generated, and run its `./verify.sh` (its CI also runs on every push).

The four-target tree checked in at
`a534c7f97ba34fd561ae03134f90b81ee4e395c1` generated and elaborated, and the
canonical local CI contexts passed.  This is not yet comparator acceptance:
all-four closure equality, equality of the private completeness auxiliaries, a
real-landrun run with nanoda, and a verified merged-`main` pin remain pending.
The only comparator acceptance recorded so far is the narrower historical run
at `4aec9ebedf6ca401e3f2d7b4bd90bd565d38f90d`, whose configuration contained
only `pauli_soundness` and `pauli_soundness_qubit` and used fake landrun.

## Maintenance notes

- A challenge's `extras`/`module_preludes` tables carry elaboration context
  (attribute commands, `CoeFun` instances, `variable`/`open` blocks) that the
  kernel closure cannot see.  Extend them if regeneration produces compile
  errors in that challenge's `Challenge.lean`; the assembler fails loudly if one
  of the challenge's own table keys no longer matches any extracted
  declaration.  The tables are per challenge, so an LDT key never constrains the
  QPBT closure or the other way round.
- A `module_preludes` entry is one scope, or a list of scopes each covering a
  line range (`first`/`last`) of its module: a module needs one scope per source
  section whose context differs.  A scope opened with `noncomputable section` in
  the source is marked `"noncomputable": true`, because the definitions inside
  such a section carry no `noncomputable` keyword of their own.
- The target statements in each footer mirror the theorems in the library:
  `challenge_footer.lean` mirrors
  `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/MainTheorem/MainFormal.lean`, and
  `challenge_qpbt_footer.lean` mirrors

  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/QubitForm.lean`.  If a library statement changes, update
  the footer too - comparator fails with "theorem statement do not match" until
  the two agree.
- Declarations without a source range (compiler-generated congruence lemmas
  and `autoParam` helpers) are emitted as explanatory comments; they

# Comparator verification of the headline theorems

Two challenges are configured, one per headline result: the LDT challenge
for `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` and the QPBT challenge for
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` and `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit`.
They share the generation tooling in `scripts/comparator/`, the drift guard
and the trust model below; each lives in its own challenge repository.

## The LDT challenge

The headline theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` (the corrected source
statement of `thm:main-formal` from the low individual degree test paper) is
independently verifiable with the official
[leanprover/comparator](https://github.com/leanprover/comparator), the
top level of the escalating checks in the Lean reference manual's
[Validating Proofs](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/ValidatingProofs/)
chapter.

Following community practice
([lamplighter-comparator](https://github.com/vidick/lamplighter-comparator),
[erdos-unit-distance-comparator](https://github.com/kim-em/erdos-unit-distance-comparator)),
the challenge lives in a separate repository —
**[LDT-comparator](https://github.com/LionSR/LDT-comparator)** —
which requires this library as a lake dependency pinned by commit:

- `Challenge.lean` there imports **only Mathlib** and re-declares, verbatim
  and in dependency order, every declaration in the comparator-relevant
  closure of the statement of `mainFormal` (111 declarations, ~1200 lines),
  then states the theorem with `sorry`.  It is the entire human audit
  surface.
- `Solution.lean` there imports this library, which proves the theorem under
  the same fully-qualified names; no bridging lemmas are needed.
- Its CI runs the comparator (real landrun sandbox, nanoda external kernel,
  `lean4checker` re-check) on every push and weekly.

## What this repository contributes

1. **Environment alignment.**  Comparator compares, constant by constant, the
   full kernel closure of the statement — types, definition bodies, and the
   proofs embedded in them — so `Challenge.lean` must elaborate to
   bit-identical terms.  Every module contributing a declaration to the
   closure therefore uses the full `import Mathlib` (directly or through
   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersBase.lean` /
   `MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`), so tactic elaboration sees
   the same environment as the Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`.  The four
   modules with direct Mathlib imports carry a comment saying not to narrow
   them.  (Measured impact: only 14 modules that did not already see full
   Mathlib through `Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean` gained it.)
2. **Regeneration tooling.**  `scripts/comparator/` holds the closure
   extractor (a Lean metaprogram mirroring comparator's `runForUsedConsts`)
   and the assembler that produce `Challenge.lean`.  After changing any
   definition in the closure: regenerate per `scripts/comparator/README.md`,
   copy the result into LDT-comparator, and bump its library pin.

## The QPBT challenge

The QPBT headline theorems `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` (`thm:pauli`) and
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` (`cor:pauli-binary`) get the same
treatment, in the separate repository
**[QPBT-comparator](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator)**.

- **Targets.**  Both theorems are verified in one comparator run
  (`theorem_names` lists both), so the challenge re-declares the union of the
  two statement closures.
- **Closure size.**  190 declarations from twenty library
  modules, about 2700 lines — larger than the LDT challenge because the
  Pauli basis test carries the full question/answer combinatorics
  (`PauliType`, `PauliAnswer`, the win predicate and the question
  distribution) into the statement.
- **Generated file.**  `scripts/comparator/expected/ChallengeQPBT.lean.expected`,
  regenerated and byte-compared by the same drift guard as the LDT challenge
  (`--challenge qpbt`).

### Environment alignment for QPBT

Comparator compares the full kernel closure constant by constant, so the
Mathlib-only challenge file must elaborate to bit-identical terms.  Two
obstacles had to be removed in the library:

1. **Narrowed imports.**  Four closure modules —
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Subspaces.lean`,
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Coefficients.lean`,
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/LowDegreeCode.lean` and
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Lines.lean` — imported individual Mathlib files, so
   tactic elaboration there saw a smaller environment than the challenge file
   would.  They now use the full `import Mathlib` and carry the same "do not
   narrow this import" comment as the LDT base modules.  The remaining sixteen
   closure modules already saw full Mathlib through
   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersBase.lean` or
   `MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`.
2. **Private closure members.**  A `private` declaration's real name is
   qualified by its defining module (`_private.<module>.0.<name>`), so a
   challenge file in a different module can never re-declare it under the
   library's name.  Nineteen closure members were private — twelve in
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/FieldBasis.lean` (the self-dual normal basis
   construction that `fixedFieldModel` selects from), six in
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Subspaces.lean` (the pivot-rank machinery behind
   `canonicalComplement`), and `singlePauliVec` in
   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Pauli.lean`.  Dropping `private` is the smallest
   faithful edit: no statement, definition body or proof script changes, only
   the visibility of names that the statement closure already depends on.

No statement of either headline theorem changed, and their axiom closure
remains `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.

The "do not narrow this import" notes on the shared base modules
(`MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersBase.lean`,
`MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/Distribution.lean`,
`MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`) still name only `mainFormal`,
and deliberately so: those modules contribute to both closures, and adding a
line to a module docstring shifts every declaration below it, which would
rewrite the `-- source:` provenance comments of the checked-in LDT challenge.
They are covered by this section instead.

In practice the\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\leanok` tag\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\n  conclusion.\n- The proof body is one of:\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\n\n### Concrete example\n\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\n\n```lean\ntheorem mainInduction\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\n```\n\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\nthe conclusion.
